Glossary

One rendering per controlled Latin term, so that what repeats in the Latin repeats in the Portuguese. Under a term: its word study, and the psalms where a decision turns on it.

One rendering per controlled Latin term, so that what repeats in the Latin repeats in the Portuguese. It grows from the work: add an entry when a word turns out to recur or to collide with a neighbour; put your psalm number beside it. Status: decided (Gustavo) · settled (ruled by Claude overnight under Gustavo's delegation, with reasons in DECISIONS.md — use it; he reviews) · working (use it; nobody has ruled) · open (no settled rendering — propose, and make it a decision in your psalm).

Heavy-duty words get a study in words/ (python3.13 research/psalterium/words.py <name> '<regex>' --greek … --pt …).

Address and grammar

Status
Godvós, lowercase pronounsdecided
plural humansvósdecided Ps 10:2 — a cost of vós found: quómodo dícitis ánimæ meæ (the advisers, plural) in a psalm that turns to God in 10:4 (perfecísti, singular): the Latin tells the two apart by number, Portuguese cannot. como dizeis à minha alma was heard by the blind reader FIRST as said to the Lord; como dizeis vós (the subject named, set against o Senhor of the first colon — D2 allows it) was heard as said to others. The same remedy may serve wherever plural men are addressed next to God (cf. D25 on 7:13). Ps 13:6 consílium ínopis confudístis (the evildoers, plural, between two verses naming the Lord in the third person): the Ps 10:2 remedy used again — vós envergonhastes (the subject named); the blind reader heard it as said to the evildoers, not to God. The remedy holds twice now.
a singular human addresseetudecided Ps 20:9–13 (after 20:8 names the king in the third person, Inveniátur manus tua … Pones eos): the addressee is God or the king, and the Latin leaves it open (20:10 then names Dóminus in the third person). Kept vós — it holds both readings; the blind reader heard the Lord throughout, with the doubt the Latin itself raises at 20:10. tu (the king) is one touch away (decision address). For Gustavo.
God speaking to a single addressee — his Anointed / Son (2:7–9), the king, the just man (90:9–13)tu — address follows the speaker: vós is the voice of the one who prays to God, not a mark of the addressee's rank; when God speaks he says tu (Tu és meu Filho, eu hoje te gerei)settled (D17); was: open — ruled in Ps 2 (decision address), wants confirming; will govern 109:1, 109:4, 88:27–28. Does not settle the psalmist addressing the Messiah-king (Ps 44). The vós form is selectable in Ps 2 (Vós sois meu Filho … Pedi-me) Ps 109 applied: 109:1a Senta-te à minha direita, 109:3 eu te gerei (echoing 2:7), 109:4 Tu és sacerdote para sempre. No reader remarked on the address.
servíre at the vós imperative (Servíte Dómino, 2:11, 99:2)Sede servos do Senhor — because the bare Servi ao Senhor is also "I served"settled (D18); was: open — wants a ruling like D13: Latinist (twice, minor) and stylist both asked for Servi ao Senhor; the object is a noun, so the enclitic exception does not apply; the run of imperatives around it (entendei … deixai-vos instruir … exultai) makes the mood plain — if the ban may yield to context, this is the verse Ps 99:2a servíte Dómino in lætítia → sede servos do Senhor com alegria — D18 followed, in the verse D18 named (Aclamai sounds first in the same verse). The Latinist (v1 and v2 gate, minor) and the stylist asked servi ao Senhor again; held, option 2. The ambiguity reader noted sede may flash as 'thirst' before the imperative is heard.
possessiveswith the article: o vosso nome, a minha almaworking
vós imperatives equal to a first-person past (ouvi, abri, parti)avoid the bare form; with an enclitic pronoun the imperative stands (Abri-me as portas da justiça, 117:19)decided (Gustavo); the enclitic exception settled (D13)

justificatiónesPs 118preceitossettled (D15)Ps 118 — words/ps118-terms.md. 29 of its 30 places are in Ps 118 (+104:45); δικαιώματα. justificações means excuses / the act of justifying in Portuguese and needs a footnote; Matos Soares never uses it; Portuguese Bibles have mandamentos e preceitos do Senhor for Luke 1:6 mandátis et justificatiónibus. præcéptumthe concordance Ps 2 Ps 7 Ps 18 Ps 93decretosettled (D19)proposed by Ps 118, which never has the word: 8× (2:6, 7:7b, 18:9, 80:5, 93:20, 98:7, 104:10, 148:6), always singular, πρόσταγμα in six of them; frees preceitos for justificatiónes. If justificatiónes moves to decretos, this returns to preceito. Ps 2:6, the first verse to meet it, rules that decreto holds: proclamando o seu decreto — a king set on Sion proclaims a decree and then quotes it (2:7); neither blind reader nor the Latinist remarked on it. Tried in the other seven places (ps002/prayed.json, decision praeceptum): it fails nowhere; 18:9 o decreto do Senhor é luminoso (the one ἐντολή) is the least natural. Ready to be settled Ps 7:7b, its second place: levantai-vos, Senhor, meu Deus, no decreto que mandastes — holds: a judicial word in a judicial psalm; the Latinist passed it twice, the blind reader heard "rise to carry out / in keeping with the decree"; the stylist asked for preceito, refused under D19. Ps 18:9 præcéptum Dómini lúcidum → o decreto do Senhor é luminoso — the list's third place, held; passed every reader. Ps 80:5 Quia præcéptum in Israël est → Porque é decreto em Israel — the list's place, held; articles dropped in v2 (the Latin has none; the stylist heard Porque é um as a smear). No reader remarked on decreto. Ps 93:20 vós que formais a fadiga no decreto — held against the stylist (v1) and the Latinist (v2 gate), who both asked for preceito; kept as an option. Ps 98:7 præcéptum quod dedit illis → o decreto que lhes deu: the Latinist asked preceito on v1 and at the v2 gate (minor); held under D19.

verbum / sermo / elóquiumthe concordance the concordance the concordance Ps 5 Ps 11 Ps 17 Ps 18 Ps 21 Ps 28 Ps 32 Ps 44 Ps 49 Ps 50 Ps 51 Ps 54 Ps 55 Ps 58 Ps 63 Ps 88 Ps 90 Ps 102 Ps 103 Ps 104 Ps 106 Ps 111 Ps 118palavra / palavra / o que dissestes in both numbers (before D26 the plural was os vossos ditos) (segundo o que dissestes, guardei o que dissestes). sermo: the main session overruled the agent's fala (D15: one Greek word, the stylist refused falas three times; verses that set the two side by side decide locally). elóquium: the noun o vosso dito failed the stylist six times out of six; the clause was the blind reader's own paraphrase and held on a second stylist pass (D16); where the singular must be a noun (118:123, 103:34, 104:19) the verse decides locally, dito availablesettled (D15, D16, D26)Ps 118 — words/ps118-terms.md. verbum and sermo are one Greek word (λόγος); elóquium is λόγιον. They meet in single verses (55:11, 102:20, 118:42 verbum + sermo; 147:4 elóquium + sermo), so three words. sermo → fala: L&S "talk, ordinary speech"; 54:22 as suas falas são mais macias que o azeite, 138:4 não há fala na minha língua. elóquium → dito: a thing uttered, God's or a man's (18:15a os ditos da minha boca); the least certain of the set — option promessa (DM1962) fits the formula secúndum elóquium tuum but not 118:67, 158, 172 nor a man's elóquia; oráculo refused (proparoxytone at ten cadences). Merging all into palavra is what Douay-Rheims, Matos Soares and DM1962 did. Heard (118:1–32): the stylist refused falas three times ("lines in a play", guardar as vossas falas "made up") and asked for palavras; the blind ambiguity reader understood it at once; ditos (118:11) drew no remark from either. falas stands under D2 — the ruling of the set most exposed to the ear. Heard (118:33–80): the singular o vosso dito was refused by the stylist in all six places (118:38, 41, 50, 58, 67, 76), each time for palavra; the blind reader understood it everywhere; see the formula row secúndum elóquium tuum. 118:42 (verbum … sermónibus) decides locally for uma palavra … nas vossas palavras. Heard (118:81–128): the clause passed the stylist twice and the blind reader (118:82 à espera do que dissestes, 118:116 segundo o que dissestes); the plural os vossos ditos was refused by the stylist twice at 118:103; the noun o dito da vossa justiça (118:123, decided locally as D16 asks) refused by him twice, understood by the blind reader; the Latinist marked the clause's past tense minor on his third reading. See the row elóquium — evidence from 118:81–128 D26 (draft 17): the clause now serves the plural too — o que dissestes in all twenty places of Ps 118 (the stylist refused ditos 8 times of 8 and passed the clause at 118:148, 158, 162 when re-read); the one noun left is 118:123 o dito da vossa justiça. Outside Ps 118 the psalm decides locally (11:7, 17:31, 104:19, 147:4 have a genitive or are subjects). Ps 11:7, the first elóquium outside Ps 118 (D26 asked for a local decision): Elóquia Dómini, elóquia casta → As palavras do Senhor são palavras puras. Why palavra here: the clause cannot repeat as a predicate (the Latin's figure is the noun said twice), so it would drop a repetition (rule 2); draft 1's Os ditos do Senhor são ditos castos was refused by the stylist ("máximas moralmente recatadas") — the ninth refusal of plural ditos, now with a genitive and an adjective — and the blind reader paraphrased it palavras puras; the psalm has no verbum or sermo, so nothing collides; DRB and MS1932 have words. The Latinist passed both drafts. 17:31 elóquia Dómini igne examináta should follow (as palavras do Senhor examinadas no fogo); 147:4 (elóquium + sermo in one verse) and 106:11 must still decide locally. Options kept in Ps 11: ditos castos / puros, the clause O que o Senhor disse é puro. Ps 17:31, as D27 ruled: as palavras do Senhor, examinadas no fogo — held; the Latinist passed it; the blind reader heard it rightly. Ps 18 has all three in eleven verses: verbum 18:3 (a palavra), 18:5 (as palavras deles); sermónes 18:4 (nem palavras); elóquia 18:15a. Draft 1 kept elóquia apart as D26's clause (E há de agradar o que disser a minha boca): the Latinist marked it MAJOR (a future act of saying the Latin lacks; erunt ut compláceant flattened) and the stylist named it the psalm's worst line; draft 2 took his line, E as palavras da minha boca serão tais que agradem — outside Ps 118 elóquia is palavras (11:7, 17:31, D27), so the psalm follows them and the three Latin words meet in one Portuguese word here. Passed three gates. Merged from a duplicate row (the word alone, working beside this settled row, 2026-09-21 review): verbum — palavra · working · Nunc dimittis (233) secúndum verbum tuum → segundo a vossa palavra (the same phrase: 118:25, 118:65, 118:107 — 118:25 now translated so, word for word); see the row verbum / sermo / elóquium Ps 32:6 Verbo Dómini cæli firmáti sunt → Pela palavra do Senhor os céus foram firmados — kept palavra, not explained (the brief); the Trinity versicle (Pent01-0) and Gregory's homily in C1.txt read Verbum as the Son, and the blind reader heard the creative word first. Pelo Verbo is option 2 in Ps 32's decision verbo. Ps 55:11 decides locally, as D15 asked: In Deo laudábo verbum, in Dómino laudábo sermónem → Em Deus louvarei a palavra, no Senhor louvarei a fala. Draft 1's a palavra … a palavra was refused by both the Latinist (minor) and the stylist (worst line: 'sounds like a copying slip'); the Greek differs here too (ῥῆμα / λόγον), D15's own test. a fala (the stylist's) over o discurso (the Latinist's, heard as an oration). 55:5 sermónes meos and 55:6 verba mea (both τοὺς λόγους μου) stay as minhas palavras; the v2 gate asked falas at 55:5 (minor) — refused under D15. So sermo is palavra and fala in one psalm: for whoever rules. Ps 102:20 faciéntes verbum illíus, ad audiéndam vocem sermónum ejus → que cumpris a sua palavra, para ouvir a voz das suas palavras — one of the verses D15 left to decide locally: the Greek repeats λόγος here too, so D15's merge holds. The stylist heard a jingle and asked do seu falar; options falas (55:11), do seu falar, ordens. Ps 103:34 Jucúndum sit ei elóquium meum → Seja-lhe agradável o que digo (a man's word; D26's clause in the present). The Latinist (twice) and the stylist asked a minha palavra; refused so that palavra stays verbum / sermo's; the stylist's weak mediant fixed by dropping eu. Ps 104:19 Elóquium Dómini inflammávit eum → A palavra do Senhor o inflamou (decision eloquium). v1 tried the clause O que o Senhor disse o inflamou to keep it apart from the verbum that ends 104:18 (até que viesse a sua palavra); the Latinist (paraphrase of a noun subject) and the stylist ("O que … o" misheard; worst line) refused it independently, so the psalm follows 11:7, 17:31, 18:15. The cost is D15's λόγος/λόγιον distinction, which is not heard across 104:18–19. The clause and O dito do Senhor are options. 104:28 sermónes suos and 104:42 verbi sancti sui → palavras / palavra. Ps 106:11 elóquia Dei → as palavras de Deus (v2, D26: the psalm decides) — draft 1 had D26's clause o que Deus disse to keep it apart from 106:20 verbum (a sua palavra); the Latinist and the stylist both asked for the plural noun, as 11:7. The merge with verbum nine verses off accepted.

ǽquitasPs 10 Ps 16 Ps 51 Ps 118equidadeworkingPs 118:40 na vossa equidade, 118:75 os vossos juízos são equidade (144, 172 to come) — the blind reader listed equidade as unknown; keeps retidão for diréctio (118:7) Ps 10:8 o seu rosto viu a equidade: listed as unknown by the blind reader twice more; kept. The row's word is now the most often unknown of the working rows; retidão is diréctio's, justiça justítia's — if it is to change, the candidate that collides with nothing is o que é reto (DRB's clause). tribulátioPs 9 Ps 21 Ps 33 Ps 45 Ps 59 Ps 107tribulaçãoworkingPs 4 Ps 31:7 a tribulatióne → contra a tribulação — applied. Ps 59:13 Da nobis auxílium de tribulatióne → Dai-nos auxílio na tribulação (MS1932): draft 1 contra a tribulação (31:7's build) was marked by the v1 Latinist as leaning to the Hebrew; the v2 gate asked for contra back. The runs contradict each other; na held, contra the option — for Gustavo. The colon is a Matins antiphon (Da nobis * Dómine auxílium de tribulatióne, Psalmi matutinum). 107:13 copies. Ps 107:13 = 59:13 copied (na tribulação). Its Latinist runs added two more proposals: v1 desde a tribulação, v2 contra a tribulação — four runs across the twins, three different fixes; held with Ps 59, for Gustavo.
mirificárePs 4 Ps 15 Ps 16 Ps 30fazer maravilhosoworking4:4, 15:3, 16:7, 30:22; must not collide with magnificáre → engrandecer Ps 15:3 mirificávit omnes voluntátes meas in eis → fez maravilhosas todas as minhas vontades neles (no subject supplied; the blind reader heard the Lord). The stylist wanted tornou maravilhosas — refused for this row (4:4), kept as an option. Ps 16:7 Mirífica misericórdias tuas (named in this row) → Fazei maravilhosas as vossas misericórdias (the imperative; the plural kept). The stylist asked for Tornai maravilhosas — the second stylist in two psalms (15:3, 16:7) to hear fazer maravilhoso as translated; refused for the row, his verb is option 3 in Ps 16. The Latinist passed it three times. For whoever rules the row: tornar maravilhoso keeps the -ficáre as well as fazer does. Ps 30:22 mirificávit misericórdiam suam mihi → fez maravilhosa a sua misericórdia para mim: the stylist again called the build a calque (mostrou de modo maravilhoso, refused, option); the blind reader did not stumble; passed the Latinist twice.

in idípsumPs 4 Ps 33 Ps 40 Ps 61 Ps 73a um só tempoopen4:9, 33:4, 40:7, 61:10, 73:6, 121:3 — may not bear one rendering everywhere Ps 33:4 et exaltémus nomen ejus in idípsum → e exaltemos juntos o seu nome (ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό, the Greek of in unum; Hebrew יחדו): persons acting together, so juntos, as in unum; a um só tempo would say simultaneity. Ruled locally under deferred D9; passed the Latinist twice, heard rightly. Proposal for the row: persons acting together → juntos; one agent or a thing → a um só tempo (4:9). Ps 40:7b et loquebátur in idípsum (one man speaking; the Greek puts ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό with the next verse's whispering) → e falava no mesmo sentido (DRB 'to the same purpose'): neither juntos (a plural) nor a um só tempo fits one speaker. Ruled locally; the blind reader heard both readings the Latin allows (the same talk; in agreement with the others); the stylist's do mesmo modo (manner) is an option; the Latinist passed it twice. Third local rendering: evidence that D9 cannot be one word. Ps 61:10 ut decípiant ipsi de vanitáte in idípsum → para que eles mesmos, pela vaidade, enganem juntos — persons acting together, as 33:4 (juntos); a um só tempo option. The purpose clause made finite after the stylist (draft 1 para eles … enganarem heard as 'for them'); mesmos = ipsi. Ps 73:6 excidérunt jánuas ejus in idípsum → cortaram juntos as suas portas — many axemen, so juntos (the 33:4 / 61:10 use); the same Greek (ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό) as 73:8 simul → juntos. v2 moved it after the verb: at the mediant the stylist heard it trailing with no clear referent.

The v2 Latinist (minor) asked louvor … louvai-o, calling it defensible; held, option. Ps 103:1b Confessiónem, et decórem induísti → Vestistes-vos de confissão e de esplendor — decided with 95:6 as that agent asked: the noun confissão in both twins (decision confessio; louvor, ação de graças, majestade options). The Latinist confirmed it twice; the blind reader found it strange, as the Latin is. Ps 110:1 Confitébor tibi, Dómine, in toto corde meo → Eu vos darei graças, Senhor, de todo o meu coração — 9:2 copied word for word in its first colon (137:1a should copy it too). The CNBB Lectionary's psalm 110(111) opens Eu agradeço a Deus de todo o coração (fetched, ps110/liturgy-br.txt), the same verb family. Ps 110:3 Conféssio et magnificéntia opus ejus → Confissão e magnificência é a sua obra — the noun follows 95:6 and 103:1b (decision v3a); the stylist asked Louvor and the ambiguity reader heard the sacrament (the known cost), refused for the twins and for laudátio → louvor in 110:10b. Bem-aventurado because feliz is first a mood today and beátus is a verdict on a life (L&S quotes Cicero's definition), because it is the one word heard as a macarism, and because it serves every construction (143:15 beátum dixérunt, 40:3 beátum fáciat); MS1932 has it in 1:1 and 2:13, Ps 118:1–2 already uses it; neither blind reader remarked on it. Cost: 5 syllables for 3, at the head of the verse where it is cheapest. Ps 6 has libertai a minha alma (this row's own alternative; DM1962's verb; safe: past libertei). Wherever a de … follows, or the object is me, arrancar is untouched. If one verb is wanted everywhere, libertar is the one that never fails; it stays apart from liberáre → livrar only by a suffix. Ps 118:153, 170 — éripe me with NO source named (Vide humilitátem meam, et éripe me; secúndum elóquium tuum éripe me): the row said that with me as object arrancar is untouched, but e arrancai-me with nothing to be torn from leaves the sentence hanging, as arrancai a minha alma did in Ps 6. Ps 118 has libertai-me in both (the Diurnal's verb at 153; safe); passed all readers. Evidence for the row's own last sentence: libertar is the verb that never fails. Ps 17:18, 30, 44, 49 — four times, each with a source named (de inimícis, a tentatióne, de contradictiónibus, a viro iníquo) → arrancar throughout; no reader remarked, and serei arrancado da tentação (17:30) was heard rightly. Ps 16:13 éripe ánimam meam ab ímpio → arrancai a minha alma do ímpio — a source named, so arrancar as the row says; no reader stumbled (the stylist wanted tirai, refused). Ps 21:9 erípiat eum (no source named; the mockers' words) → que ele o liberte — the row's own conclusion (libertar never fails), with livrar left to 21:5 liberásti. Mt 27:43 (Vulgate, fetched) has liberet nunc, si vult eum — another wording. See the new row éruere. Ps 30:16 Éripe me de manu inimicórum meórum → Arrancai-me da mão dos meus inimigos (a source named); no reader remark. Ps 33:5 ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus meis erípuit me → e me arrancou de todas as minhas tribulações (draft 2 the verb first, the stylist's rhyme); 33:8 erípiet eos → e os libertará. Passed the Latinist twice. 90:15 erípiam eum → eu o libertarei (Ps 90 draft 3, review 2026-09-21): the one place left with arrancar and no source; its decision had argued that na tribulação supplies one, before the evidence above existed. Ps 55:13 eripuísti ánimam meam de morte, et pedes meos de lapsu → arrancastes a minha alma da morte, e os meus pés da queda — sources named, so arrancar; no reader remarked. 114:8 (erípuit ánimam meam de morte … pedes meos a lapsu) should copy it. Ps 49:22 et non sit qui erípiat → e não haja quem liberte — no source, no object: the row's libertar. The Latinist and the stylist both asked livre (liberáre's word) — refused; arranque (the row's other verb; the snatching image) and livre kept as options. Ps 63:2 a timóre inimíci éripe ánimam meam → arrancai a minha alma do temor do inimigo — a source named, so arrancar; no reader remarked (libertai the option). Ps 58:2, 58:3 Éripe me de inimícis meis … de operántibus iniquitátem → Arrancai-me dos meus inimigos … dos que praticam a iniquidade — the row applied twice, apart from 58:2b líbera me → livrai-me; 58:2 is the Passiontide versicle (Preces, Quad5-5) and each colon stands alone. No reader remarked. Ps 68:15 Éripe me de luto → Arrancai-me da lama; 68:19 propter inimícos meos éripe me → libertai-me (no source) — the gate Latinist (minor) asked arrancai-me for one verb; held under the row. Ps 70:1 et éripe me → e libertai-me (no source; beside líbera me → livrai-me, two Greek verbs); 70:4 éripe me de manu peccatóris → arrancai-me da mão do pecador (source named); 70:11 non est qui erípiat → não há quem liberte (= 49:22, no object supplied; the v1 stylist asked o liberte, held, option). Ps 81:4 Erípite páuperem: * et egénum de manu peccatóris liberáte → Arrancai o pobre: * e livrai o necessitado … — draft 1 Libertai (no source in the colon) drew a Latinist minor: libertai … livrai sound like one verb where the Latin has two. The source da mão do pecador is in the same verse (ἐκ χειρὸς between the two Greek verbs), so the row's arrancar applies; passed the gate. Ps 106:6, 20 erípuit eos de … → os arrancou de — kept apart from liberávit (livrou, 106:13, 19) and edúxit (tirou, 106:28), as the Latin varies the refrain's verb.

The apposition laus Israël → vós, louvor de Israel: bare, it was heard as the holy place's name. Ps 23:3 in loco sancto ejus → no seu lugar santo. The row stands where in sancto is plainly a place (19:3, 21:4). Ps 62:3 sic in sancto appárui tibi → assim no lugar santo me apresentei a vós — the row; no reader remarked. Ps 67:18 in Sina in sancto, 67:25 qui est in sancto → no lugar santo (beside a place name / after está); no remark. Ps 76:14 Deus, in sancto via tua → Deus, no santo está o vosso caminho (v2): draft 1 no lugar santo (read as a place by 76:20's In mari via tua) was marked by the Latinist as closing the ambiguity; taken, as 59:8. The copula supplied so that the bare neuter can stand as a versicle (Psalmi matutinum: V. Deus, in sancto via tua. R. Quis Deus magnus sicut Deus noster).

Ps 7:9b Julgai-me, Senhor, segundo a minha justiça (= 25:1's opening), 7:8b o Senhor julga os povos — here the sense is plainly "do me justice"; no reader heard condemnation. Ps 118:154 Júdica judícium meum: Julgai o meu juízo was heard by the blind reader FIRST as "evaluate the opinion I formed" (o meu julgamento runs the same risk). Now Julgai em juízo a minha causa (from the stylist): the law-word and the figure kept, the right sense heard; passed the Latinist twice. Cost: causa is another Latin word — 9:5 judícium meum et causam meam and 34:23 set the two side by side and must decide locally. Ps 81 has the root four times (dijúdicat, judicátis, judicáte, júdica) and all four are julgar. 81:3 Judicáte egéno, et pupíllo → Julgai em favor do necessitado e do órfão = 9:39's dative build. 81:2 judicátis iniquitátem (internal accusative) → julgais com iniquidade: julgais a iniquidade would be heard as condemning it. 81:8 Surge, Deus, júdica terram → Levantai-vos, Deus, julgai a terra. No reader remarked.

Passed the Latinist twice; no other reader remarked. Ps 20:2 = 20:14a in virtúte tua → no vosso poder; 20:14b the plural virtútes tuas → os vossos poderes (the Latinist's MAJOR on the singular ao vosso poder: plural, and the object sung, not the addressee). Ps 21:16 Áruit tamquam testa virtus mea (ἰσχύς) → O meu vigor secou-se como um caco: a man's bodily strength drying up — poder would be authority, força is fortitúdo's. MS1932's vigor. Proposal: virtus of a man's own strength → vigor (30:11 infirmáta est … virtus mea, 37:11 dereliquit me virtus mea, 70:9 dum defécerit virtus mea — grep before use); poder stays for God's (in virtúte tua) and for 17:33, 40. Passed the Latinist twice; no reader remarked. Ps 23:10 Dóminus virtútum → o Senhor dos poderes (its first place of 16: 45:8, 45:12, 47:9, 58:6, 67:13 Rex virtútum, 68:7, 79:5, 8, 15, 20, 83:2, 4, 9, 13, 88:9 — grep); the plural as 20:14b. Passed the Latinist twice; the blind reader heard 'the Lord who has all powers' (or 'of powerful beings' — the Greek's δυνάμεις, the hosts, are both). Options dos exércitos (DRB, the Hebrew's Sabaoth), das virtudes (MS1932). Formula row proposed; wants a ruling before Ps 45. Ps 28:4 Vox Dómini in virtúte → A voz do Senhor com poder; 28:11 Dóminus virtútem pópulo suo dabit → O Senhor dará poder ao seu povo (God's virtus given; one word for the psalm's two places). Passed the Latinist twice; no reader remarked; the stylist named 28:11 the best line. força (DRB) the option. Ps 29:8 præstitísti decóri meo virtútem → destes vigor ao meu esplendor — the proposal vigor for a man's strength applied (given by God to the man's decor, not God's own power); passed the Latinist twice; poder the option. Ps 37:11 derelíquit me virtus mea → abandonou-me o meu vigor — the proposal vigor applied at a place it named; passed the Latinist twice, no reader remarked. Ps 45:2 Deus noster refúgium, et virtus → O nosso Deus é refúgio e poder — God's virtus → poder, kept apart from 45:4 in fortitúdine ejus → força two verses later; the familiar refúgio e força (MS1932, DRB) is the option. Passed the Latinist twice. Ps 43:10 the plural of the people's hosts in virtútibus nostris → com as nossas forças (v2): draft 1 poderes was heard abstract by the blind reader, and the Latinist and the stylist asked forças independently. See the row virtútes nostræ. Ps 47:14 in virtúte ejus (Sion's strength, αὐτῆς) → no seu poder — a city's virtus, which the row did not cover; força (MS1932, DRB) the option. Passed the Latinist twice. Ps 64:7 Prǽparans montes in virtúte tua, accínctus poténtia → Vós que preparais os montes com o vosso poder, cingido de potência — the instrumental in as com (the stylist heard no vosso poder as locative); the formula keeps no where it is locative (20:2, 53:3). poténtia in the same verse → potência (new row). Ps 70:9 cum defécerit virtus mea (ἰσχύς, a man's strength) → quando desfalecer o meu vigor, as 21:16, 30:11b, 37:11. Ps 83:8 ibunt de virtúte in virtútem → irão de virtude em virtude (decision devirtute) — a local departure: DRB and MS1932 both say virtue; Portuguese virtude still holds 'power, efficacy', so it keeps the Latin's double sense (strength and excellence). Cost: the echo with Senhor dos poderes four times in the same psalm is lost; de poder em poder (the row) and de força em força are options. The ambiguity reader heard moral virtue first. For Gustavo. Ps 101:24 in via virtútis suæ → no caminho do seu vigor — the row's proposal for a man's strength (the one who answers); the ambiguity reader heard 'while still strong'. força, poder options. Ps 102:20 poténtes virtúte (δυνατοὶ ἰσχύι, the angels) → poderosos em força — v1 had the proposal's vigor; the stylist heard poderosos em vigor as a tautology. A local departure (no fortitúdo in the psalm); vigor the option. 102:21 omnes virtútes ejus → todos os seus poderes (D43's plural); the ambiguity reader heard abstract powers, not heavenly beings — exércitos (DRB) the option.

Ps 18:13 et ab aliénis parce servo tuo → e dos alheios poupai o vosso servo — three drafts: das estranhas (draft 1, the faults of others with faltas understood) failed three readers at once (Latinist MAJOR, the stylist, the blind reader, all hearing 'odd faults'); das alheias (draft 2) failed the gate MAJOR because 18:14b's masculine domináti makes its subject persons (delícta would give domináta); dos estranhos (draft 3, persons) failed the gate MAJOR for closing out others' faults. dos alheios (the Latinist's fix twice) holds both, as the masculine/neuter aliénis does, and passed. So: estranho for persons named as such (17:46 filhos estranhos); a bare substantival aliéni may want os alheios. Ps 57:4 Alienáti sunt peccatóres → os pecadores se fizeram estranhos — the verb kept in this row's family; the cognate se alienaram is modern jargon. Tried on 22:5 Preparastes à minha vista uma mesa, 137:1b À vista dos anjos, 115:15 Preciosa à vista do Senhor — it fails none. In Ps 5 it stays apart from astábo tibi → diante de vós and ante óculos tuos → diante dos vossos olhos. The blind reader heard "make my conduct right in your eyes" first. Options na vossa presença, diante de vós. Ps 118:168–170 — in conspéctu tuo three verses running, two of them with a verb of MOTION (Appropínquet … in conspéctu tuo, Intret … in conspéctu tuo): à vossa vista is excellent in 118:168 (todos os meus caminhos estão à vossa vista) and impossible in 118:170 (Entre o meu pedido à vossa vista). Ps 118 has the noun phrase a vossa presença in all three, each verb taking its own preposition (estão na … · Aproxime-se … da … · Entre … na … — the stylist refused Aproxime-se na); passed thereafter. For whoever studies the 51 verses: à vista de fails with verbs of motion. Ps 9:20 in conspéctu tuo → à vossa vista, 9:26a Non est Deus in conspéctu ejus → Não há Deus à vista dele: the noun kept; the blind reader heard 9:26a as 'God does not count for him' — the sense. Evidence for vista over diante de. Ps 14:4a in conspéctu ejus → À vista dele: the stylist asked for Aos olhos dele ('à vista' sounded like physical presence) — refused, olho is óculus's; the blind reader heard 'aos olhos do homem descrito', the judging look, rightly. Evidence for vista again (9:20, 9:26a, 14:4a). Ps 17 has in conspéctu four times in 17:2–25 (one decision conspectu): à vista de where it is a predicate (17:23 todos os seus juízos estão à minha vista; 17:25 à vista dos seus olhos), na sua presença where it hangs beside a noun (17:7b o meu clamor, na sua presença, entrou nos seus ouvidos; 17:13 Diante do clarão, na sua presença, passaram as nuvens). In 17:13 the genitive o clarão da sua presença was refused by the Latinist (major): the phrase is adverbial, not the brightness's owner. Evidence that à vista serves predicates, presença the rest. Ps 15:8 Providébam Dóminum in conspéctu meo semper → Eu via o Senhor sempre à minha vista (the Latinist's line); the stylist's diante de mim refused for this row's noun, kept as an option. Acts 2:25 quotes it (fetched). Ps 16:15 apparébo conspéctui tuo (a dative, no in) → aparecerei à vossa vista — the row's noun as a predicate place; the blind reader heard 'appear before God as a just man'. Ps 21 (one decision conspectu, three slots): 21:26 vota mea reddam in conspéctu timéntium eum → à vista dos que o temem (the place of witnesses); 21:28b adorábunt in conspéctu ejus and 21:30 in conspéctu ejus cadent → na sua presença (with an act of worship; adorarão à vista dele is stiff) — the Ps 17 split again. No reader remarked. Ps 22:5 in conspéctu meo → à minha vista (the row's noun, as 5:9's à vista de). Ps 35:3 in conspéctu ejus → à sua vista (whose — God's or his own — left open, as the Latin; the blind reader heard God's). Ps 55:9 posuísti lácrimas meas in conspéctu tuo → pusestes as minhas lágrimas à vossa vista (the Wednesday Matins versicle's response); à vista de applied; the stylist named 55:9 the psalm's best line. Ps 49:3b in conspéctu ejus → na sua presença; 49:8 in conspéctu meo → na minha presença (God's sight: as 17:13, 21:30); à vista dele / à minha vista options. Ps 60:8 Pérmanet in ætérnum in conspéctu Dei → Ele permanece para sempre na presença de Deus (abiding before God, as 49:8); à vista de Deus the option. Ps 67:4, 5b exsúltent in conspéctu Dei → exultem na presença de Deus (joy, not being watched); 67:8 egrederéris in conspéctu pópuli tui → saíeis à vista do vosso povo. No remark. Ps 79:10 Dux itíneris fuísti in conspéctu ejus → diante dela — a local departure (draft 1 had à vista dela): the stylist heard à vista first as 'in cash' and bureaucratic, the ambiguity reader lost the link of dela to the vine; the Greek is ἔμπροσθεν. Evidence against à vista de with a third-person pronoun; à vista remains an option there. Passed the Latinist. Ps 85:14 et non proposuérunt te in conspéctu suo → e não vos puseram diante da sua vista (53:5's words). The stylist called it a calque and asked diante dos seus olhos — refused, olho is óculus's and 53:5 is the twin; an option in Ps 85's conspectu. Ps 95:6 in conspéctu ejus with a copula → estão na sua presença (21:28b, 49:3b): estão à vista dele would be heard as 'are visible to him'. à vista dele, diante dele options. Ps 97 (one decision conspectu, three slots): 97:2 in conspéctu géntium → à vista das nações (witnesses of a revelation); 97:6 Jubiláte in conspéctu regis Dómini → Aclamai na presença do rei, o Senhor (acclamation, as 67:4); 97:8 a conspéctu Dómini (the only a conspéctu, πρὸ προσώπου) → à vista do Senhor (MS1932's words). No reader objected; the ambiguity reader heard 97:8 as 'in the Lord's presence'. Ps 99:2b Introíte in conspéctu ejus → Entrai na sua presença — a verb of motion, as 118:170; no reader remarked. Ps 115 (one decision conspectu): 115:5b pretiósa in conspéctu Dómini → é preciosa à vista do Senhor (the test this row named; aos olhos MS1932 option — olho is óculus's); 115:9 in conspéctu omnis pópuli ejus → à vista de todo o seu povo (21:26's formula, the place of witnesses), against 115:5a coram omni pópulo ejus → diante de todo o seu povo. The Latinist praised the kept coram / in conspéctu split twice; the ambiguity reader heard 'in the Lord's sight' first.
adjuvárePs 39 Ps 45 Ps 53 Ps 69 Ps 78 Ps 118auxiliar (Deus me auxilia)openPs 53:6; keeps one family with adjutórium → auxílio and adjútor (117:7 next); plainer alternative ajudar splits the family. Ps 118:86, 117 auxiliai-me (safe at the imperative); no reader remarked Ps 21:12 non est qui ádjuvet → não há quem auxilie (no object, as the Latin); no reader remarked. Ps 39:14b Dómine, ad adjuvándum me réspice → Senhor, olhai para auxiliar-me (draft 1 para me auxiliar was heard 'look at me' by the stylist; the enclitic after the infinitive mends it). This is the half that Ps 69:2b shares (Dómine, ad adjuvándum me festína, the response of every Hour's opening versicle): it fixes auxiliar-me there, not inténde in adjutórium (D40, deferred). The stylist's olhai em meu auxílio refused: adjutórium's noun, and it would pre-empt D40. Ps 45:6 adjuvábit eam Deus → Deus há de auxiliá-la — draft 1 Deus a auxiliará lost the object in choir (a au-, the stylist); the periphrastic future keeps the enclitic audible. Ps 69:2b Dómine, ad adjuvándum me festína → Senhor, apressai-vos para auxiliar-me (39:14b's phrase kept whole; para, not 30:3's a, to avoid a au-); 69:6 Deus, ádjuva me → Deus, auxiliai-me — the stylist asked socorrei-me (heavy at the urgent cry): refused, it breaks the psalm's adjuvándum … ádjuva … Adjútor echo; option adjuva. No reader remarked on 69:2b. Ps 78:9 Ádjuva nos → Auxiliai-nos (as 43:26); the stylist asked Ajudai-nos — refused for the family, option adjuva.

Desviar keeps avértere one verb with or without a dative; the Latinist passed it twice. Ps 13:7 cum avérterit Dóminus captivitátem plebis suæ → quando o Senhor afastar o cativeiro do seu povo: draft 1 had this row's desviar; the stylist found desviar o cativeiro not Portuguese and the blind reader could not tell whether the captivity was present or threatened. Afastar (the stylist's) taken there — it shares a verb with amovére / repéllere (row amovére), which never meet captivitátem. Desviar stays right with a face (12:1) or anger (77:38, 105:24 ut avérteret iram). 84:2 avertísti captivitátem Jacob should follow Ps 13 (afastastes o cativeiro de Jacó). The twin 52:7 has convérterit (row convértere) and should differ. Ps 21:25b Nec avértit fáciem suam a me → Nem desviou de mim a sua face (the face formula, 12:1). Ps 84:2, 84:4, 84:5 — afastar all three times (afastastes o cativeiro de Jacó; afastastes-vos da ira da vossa indignação, reflexive because the Latin has no object; e afastai de nós a vossa ira, the Compline response): one verb for the psalm's one verb, three times in four verses (rule 6), where this row would give desviar for anger (77:38b). MS1932 afasta de nós a tua ira. Cost: avértere iram is afastar here, desviar at 77:38b. The split is option 1 of Ps 84's avertere. Both Latinist gates passed it. Ps 89:3 Ne avértas hóminem in humilitátem → Não desvieis o homem para a humilhação (no dative; in + accusative) — the ambiguity reader heard moral disgrace as well as lowliness; reduzais (MS1932) option. The play avértas / Convertímini is lost.

Ps 17:41 et odiéntes me disperdidísti → e exterminastes os que me odeiam. Ps 36:9 exterminabúntur (exterminári, ἐξολεθρευθήσονται) → serão exterminados — the cognate, shared with dispérdere: the two never meet in a verse (exterminári only 36:9, 79:14, grep). adjútorPs 7 Ps 9 Ps 17 Ps 18 Ps 26 Ps 27 Ps 29 Ps 32 Ps 34 Ps 37 Ps 39 Ps 45 Ps 51 Ps 61 Ps 69 Ps 70 Ps 71 Ps 80 Ps 82 Ps 88 Ps 90 Ps 108 Ps 113 Ps 117 Ps 118auxílio (O Senhor é o meu auxílio)open — for Gustavo (HANDOFF). The text is uniform, auxílio 14/14; D19 names adjútor → auxílio only in passing, as what amparo stays apart from — it is not a ruling, so the row stays openPs 117:6–7; one family with adjutórium and adjuváre; the Latinist asked twice (minor) for the agent noun auxiliador — refused for length and currency, kept as an option; the same metonymy as suscéptor → amparo. Ps 118:114 Vós sois o meu auxílio e o meu amparo: the Latinist asked for auxiliador … protetor three times — minor, then MAJOR twice with the text unchanged; refused each time (protetor is protéctor's; D19) — the final text stands against the gate there Ps 9:10, 9:35b auxílio … vós sereis auxílio para o órfão: the Latinist marked 9:10 MAJOR twice (drafts 2 and 3) for auxiliador; held on purpose (D24), his word is the option in Ps 9's decision adjutor. Ps 17:3b O meu Deus é o meu auxílio: the Latinist asked for auxiliador again — minor on draft 1, MAJOR on draft 2 with the words unchanged; held (D24), recorded in Ps 17's decision adjutor. Ps 17:2–3 sets four agent nouns side by side (liberátor, adjútor, protéctor, suscéptor): the Portuguese makes two agents (libertador, protetor) and two abstracts (auxílio, amparo). If Gustavo wants the series regular, Ps 17's decisions adjutor and susceptor turn both in one touch each. Ps 18:15b Dómine, adjútor meus, et redémptor meus → Senhor, meu auxílio, e meu redentor — HELD against four Latinist MAJORS (drafts 1–4), each asking meu auxiliador: here the agent noun redentor stands beside it and the metonymy is most exposed (77:35 has the same pair, Deus adjútor est eórum: et Deus excélsus redémptor eórum est). Held for D19 and the psalter's one word; needs a ruling — proposal: keep auxílio in the formula places (O Senhor é o meu auxílio) but allow auxiliador where adjútor is paired with another agent noun (18:15b, 77:35), or settle auxílio everywhere and record the gate's objection as D24 does. Ps 29:11 Dóminus factus est adjútor meus → o Senhor se fez o meu auxílio — HELD against two Latinist MAJORS (drafts 1 and 2) asking auxiliador, as 9:10 (se fez refúgio … auxílio), 17:19's build (se fez o meu protetor). No reader misheard it. Another place for the ruling this row asks. Ps 26:9b Adjútor meus esto → Sede o meu auxílio (a versicle, 05-01r.txt) — the Latinist's MAJOR auxiliador held again (D19/D24), as at 29:11. 27:7 (minor) the same. Ps 27:7 Dóminus adjútor meus … et adjútus sum → O Senhor é o meu auxílio … e fui auxiliado — the Latinist's remark (minor on draft 1, MAJOR on the gate) held (D19/D24). Ps 32:20 quóniam adjútor et protéctor noster est → porque o nosso auxílio e protetor é ele — HELD against two Latinist MAJORS (drafts 1 and 2) asking o nosso auxiliador e protetor. Here adjútor is paired with the agent noun protéctor — exactly the case this row's standing proposal names (with 18:15b, 77:35); add 32:20 to that list. auxiliador is option 2 in Ps 32's decision adjutor. Ps 39:18b Adjútor meus, et protéctor meus tu es → Vós sois o meu auxílio e o meu protetor (= 27:7's words; the pair with an agent noun again). The Latinist passed it twice this time; the stylist failed it ('an abstract noun beside a person-noun, the pair limps') and offered socorro / amparo — refused (socorro is as abstract; amparo is suscípere's, 39:12). 69:6b Adjútor meus, et liberátor meus es tu will copy the first half. Ps 51:8 qui non pósuit Deum adjutórem suum → que não fez de Deus o seu auxílio — the Latinist asked for the agent noun on both runs (minor: auxiliador, then ajudador); held for this row. Ps 61:7 adjútor meus → o meu auxílio, 61:9 Deus adjútor noster → Deus é o nosso auxílio — the Latinist asked ajudador on both runs (major at v1 on 61:7, bundled with the voice fault; minor at v2), noting 61:8 Deus auxílii mei → o Deus do meu auxílio makes the two Latin words one; held for this row, decision adjutor records the option. Ps 69:6b Adjútor meus, et liberátor meus es tu → Vós sois o meu auxílio e o meu libertador (39:18b's first half copied) — beside the agent noun libertador, the row's hard case again; the Latinist asked auxiliador on both runs (minor); held, option in decision adjutor. Add 69:6b to the list of paired places (18:15b, 32:20, 39:18b, 77:35). Ps 70:7 et tu adjútor fortis → e vós sois um auxílio forte (no reader remarked this time); 70:12 in auxílium meum is auxílium's own noun. Ps 71:12 et páuperem, cui non erat adjútor → e o pobre que não tinha quem o auxiliasse — a local departure from auxílio: the v1 Latinist and stylist both asked for the person (quem o ajudasse); taken in the row's own verb (adjuváre → auxiliar) because here there is no meus formula, only a man without a helper. auxílio, auxiliador options. The gate passed it. Ps 80:2 Deo, adjutóri nostro → Deus, nosso auxílio — the row; the v2 Latinist asked auxiliador (minor), held for the row; option. Ps 108:12 Non sit illi adjútor → Não haja quem o auxilie — a local departure (decision adjutor): the v1 Latinist and stylist both asked for the person, and the clause gives the Latin's Non sit … nec sit qui its parallel. auxílio para ele the option. Ps 113:17–19 adjútor eórum et protéctor eórum est (×3) → ele é o auxílio deles e o protetor deles — the Latinist asked (minor) for the agent noun at v1 (auxiliador) and again at the v2 gate (ajudador); refused on this row, kept as an option. The mixed abstract/agent pair is the row's known cost.

exquírerePs 118procuraropenPs 118:2, 10, 22 (8× in the psalm); kept apart from quǽrere → buscar (118:100, 118:176 quære servum tuum) and requírere (118:145, not yet met); MS1932 merges into buscar 118:145 requíram is merged into it (procurarei os vossos preceitos): the Greek is ἐκζητήσω, the very verb behind exquírere all eight times in the psalm, so the variation is the Latin's elegance (D15's test) and Portuguese has no plain third verb (requerer is to petition an office). Ps 13:2 aut requírens Deum (ἐκζητῶν, = 52:3b, = Rom 3:11) → ou quem procure a Deus: requírere merged into this row's verb again, on the Greek, as at 118:145; busque (MS1932, DM1962) is the option. 9:13 requírens sánguinem (God, of blood) stays pedir contas. Ps 110:2 exquisíta in omnes voluntátes ejus → procuradas segundo todas as suas vontades (the participle keeps the row; DRB 'sought out according to'). The two Latinist runs contradicted each other on in (v1 em, v2 segundo); the stylist found procuradas opaque (worst line) and asked primorosas segundo — refused (the adjectival 'exquisite' sense, dropping the seeking of ἐξεζητημένα), option.

confúndiPs 30 Ps 33 Ps 34 Ps 39 Ps 68 Ps 70 Ps 96 Ps 118ser envergonhado; active não me envergonheissettled (D15)Ps 118:6, 31 (also 46, 78, 80, 116). Draft 1 had the traditional ser confundido; the blind reader heard "I shall not be confused" first in both verses, so it was changed. Costs for Gustavo to weigh: 30:2 = 70:1 non confúndar in ætérnum (the last line of the Te Deum) would not be the traditional não serei confundido; and erubéscere, which stands beside confúndi in 34:4/26, 39:15, 69:3–4, needs another word — proposed corar Ps 6:11 is the first erubéscere, and corar holds: Que todos os meus inimigos corem … e corem muito depressa — the Latin's own image (to redden), bare; the blind reader took it at once for shame, the stylist kept it twice in his own rebuilt line, the Latinist passed it. See the new row erubéscere. Ps 13:6 the active with men as subject, consílium ínopis confudístis → vós envergonhastes o conselho do indigente: D15's verb holds in the active; the Latinist passed it twice, the blind reader heard 'put to shame' without remark (he heard conselho as advice given). Ps 21:6 non sunt confúsi → não foram envergonhados (D15); heard as 'not humiliated'. Ps 24:3 não serão envergonhados, 24:4 Sejam envergonhados (beside erubéscere → corar in 24:1, 24:20). Ps 30:2 and 30:17 — the Te Deum line, decided here as D15 foresaw: In te, Dómine, sperávi, non confúndar in ætérnum → Em vós, Senhor, esperei: para sempre não serei envergonhado; 30:17 Dómine, non confúndar → Senhor, não serei envergonhado (one decision, confundar). confúndar is future and present subjunctive at once; the Greek has the optative (μὴ καταισχυνθείην) both times and DRB / MS1932 take the wish — the future is ruled, as 24:1 não corarei, with D23's formula for the negated in ætérnum. The blind reader heard 'never be put to shame'; the Latinist passed both places twice. The stylist asked não serei envergonhado para sempre (the 'not for ever' order, refused; option). Options: jamais, the wish não seja eu envergonhado, the traditional confundido. = 70:1 and the Te Deum's close (Common/Prayers.txt). Ps 34:4 Confundántur et revereántur → Sejam envergonhados e desonrados; 34:4b confundántur → sejam envergonhados; 34:26b confusióne → de vergonha. reveréri beside it needed a third word (new row). Ps 52:6b confúsi sunt, quóniam Deus sprevit eos → foram envergonhados, porque Deus os desprezou (D15). The stylist asked ficaram envergonhados («stiff, bookish passive») — refused, option: ficar envergonhado is a feeling, confúsi sunt is being put to shame; the Latinist passed it twice. Ps 70:1 = 30:2a copied (para sempre não serei envergonhado, decision confundar with Ps 30's options). The v1 Latinist asked the wish (que eu não seja envergonhado para sempre) and the v1 stylist the 'not for ever' order again — both held for identical Latin, options 3 and 5. 70:13 Confundántur → Sejam envergonhados; 70:24 cum confúsi … fúerint → quando forem envergonhados. Ps 96:7 Confundántur omnes, qui adórant sculptília → Sejam envergonhados todos os que … (34:4's jussive). The stylist found the periphrastic passive heavy in a long colon (+7) and asked Envergonhem-se — refused for the row, option (confundantur).

oppróbrium / exprobrárePs 14 Ps 21 Ps 30 Ps 38 Ps 43 Ps 56 Ps 68 Ps 78 Ps 88 Ps 118afronta / afrontaropenPs 118:22; draft 1 opróbrio (MS1932, DM1962) failed both blind readers; keeps 68:10 oppróbria exprobrántium → as afrontas dos que vos afrontam; option desonra (stylist) Ps 14:3b oppróbrium non accépit advérsus próximos suos → não aceitou afronta contra os seus próximos: heard by the blind reader as 'did not tolerate offences against his neighbours' first and 'did not take up an accusation against them' second (the Latin's letter); passed the Latinist twice. Ps 21:7 oppróbrium hóminum → a afronta dos homens; heard as insult suffered. Ps 30:12 factus sum oppróbrium → tornei-me uma afronta; the blind reader heard 'someone who offends' first, 'an object of scorn' second. Super omnes inimícos meos → Mais que todos os meus inimigos (the Latinist, minor: the comparison). Ps 38:9 oppróbrium insipiénti dedísti me → fizestes de mim a afronta do insensato — draft 1 uma afronta para o insensato: the blind reader could not tell the direction; the stylist asked for a genitive (and opróbrio, refused per this row). The gate (minor) wanted the dative and dar back (destes-me como afronta ao insensato) — held: afronta ao X is heard as an insult offered to X. Option in Ps 38 dedisti. Ps 41:11 exprobravérunt mihi → afrontaram-me (heard as insulted, the blind reader). Ps 68:8, 10, 11, 20, 21 applied, and impropérium (68:20, 68:21; the same Greek ὀνειδισμός) shares afronta (D15); 68:10 oppróbria exprobrántium tibi → as afrontas dos que vos afrontam — the stylist's best line. Ps 78:4 Facti sumus oppróbrium vicínis nostris → Tornamo-nos uma afronta para os nossos vizinhos (43:14's words). 78:12 impropérium ipsórum, quod exprobravérunt tibi → a afronta com que eles vos afrontaram — the stylist heard a same-root jingle and asked insultaram: refused, the Greek has the figure (ὀνειδισμὸν … ὠνείδισαν), as 68:10; option.
contémptusPs 118desprezoworkingPs 118:22 Ps 21:7 abjéctio plebis (only here) → o desprezo do povo: its Greek ἐξουδένημα is of the root of 118:22 ἐξουδένωσιν (contémptum) and of 21:25 ἐξουδένωσεν (non sprevit → não desprezou), so the psalm's own echo is kept. Options o refugo, MS1932 a abjeção.
declináre aPs 13 Ps 16 Ps 20 Ps 36 Ps 43 Ps 54 Ps 100 Ps 118apartar-se deopenPs 118:21 (also 51, 102, 157; 118:115 Apartai-vos de mim, malignos); keeps desviar for avértere Ps 13:3a Omnes declinavérunt (absolute; = 52:4 = Rom 3:12) → Todos se desviaram: without a, and next to juntos (simul), se apartaram risks 'they parted from one another'; the reflexive desviar-se is not avértere's transitive desviar. The blind reader heard 'turned from the good'. Absolute declinavérunt elsewhere (20:12, 54:4 in me, 101:12 of days like a shadow) is another build; 77:57 avertérunt se will also be se desviaram — two Latin verbs share a form there. Transitive, declináre in + object: Ps 20:12 declinavérunt in te mala → voltaram males contra vós (the stylist's worst line was desviaram males contra vós); the twin 54:4 declinavérunt in me iniquitátes should follow (voltaram iniquidades contra mim). voltar is also convértere's — they do not meet in these lines. Ps 33:15 Divérte a malo, et fac bonum → Aparta-te do mal, e faz o bem — another verb (divértere, ἔκκλινον as in 36:27), the same image, so this row's apartar-se de. 36:27 Declína a malo, et fac bonum is the near twin (one Greek) — it should copy the colon. Ps 36:27a Declína a malo, et fac bonum → Aparta-te do mal, e faz o bem (= 33:15a, the formula row); passed the Latinist twice. Ps 54:4 departs from the wording foreseen here: declinavérunt in me iniquitátes → Porque as iniquidades se voltaram contra mim (v2). All three v1 readers heard bare voltaram iniquidades contra mim as "came back, returned"; the reflexive says "turned against". The object reading (LXX, DRB cast) survives only as the option lançaram. 20:12 voltaram males contra vós carries the same risk — for review. Passed the Latinist gate. Ps 100:4 declinántem a me malígnum → o malvado que se apartava de mim (D24 with this row).

So in 17:22 nec ímpie gessi a Deo meo took apartar-se (e não me apartei impiamente do meu Deus — the Latinist's major, taken) to keep the two verbs apart. Ps 38:10 ámove a me plagas tuas → afastai de mim os vossos flagelos (= 118:29's verb). Ps 65:20 qui non amóvit oratiónem meam → que não afastou a minha oração — applied; no remark.
adhærérePs 72 Ps 93apegar-se aopenPs 118:25 A minha alma apegou-se ao chão, 118:31 Apeguei-me aos vossos testemunhos (one verb twice in the stanza); fits 62:9 Adhǽsit ánima mea post te, 21:16, 72:28; MS1932 aderir, DM1962 colar-se Ps 21:16 lingua mea adhǽsit fáucibus meis → a minha língua se colou à minha garganta — a physical sticking: se apegou (draft 1, this row) was heard by the stylist as affection before touch, so the row's own option (DM1962 colar-se) is taken there. Ps 24:21 Os inocentes e os retos apegaram-se a mim (the blind reader heard affection first, support second). Ps 62:8b adhǽsit ánima mea post te → a minha alma apegou-se a vós, seguindo-vos — post te kept by a participle (the Latinist's v1 fix; on the v2 gate he asked atrás de vós, held as unidiomatic; option). The colon is the antiphon of St Stephen / St Lawrence. Ps 72:28 Mihi autem adhærére Deo bonum est → Mas para mim é bom apegar-me a Deus — applied as the row names; the versicle read alone; passed every reader. Ps 93:20 Numquid adhæret tibi sedes iniquitatis → Acaso se apega a vós o trono da iniquidade. Ps 100:4 Non adhǽsit mihi cor pravum → Não se apegou a mim coração perverso. Ps 101:6 adhǽsit os meum carni meæ → os meus ossos se colaram à minha carne — colar-se as proposed; the collective singular made plural (the Latinist, minor on v1 and the v2 gate, asked o meu osso: held, heard as one bone; option). The stylist asked aderiram (option).

Ps 7:10 díriges justum → e dirigireis o justo: a future, which the ban does not reach; with a person as object it says "guide, steer" (DRB direct). Passed all three readers; options encaminhareis (MS1932), endireitareis. Ps 58:5 absolute diréxi → segui reto (the stylist's, for draft 1 segui direito); no object supplied. The Latinist (v2, minor) asked dirigi os meus passos (DRB, MS1932) — option. Ps 100:7 intransitive non diréxit in conspéctu oculórum meórum → não seguiu reto à vista dos meus olhos, = 58:5 segui reto; held against the stylist's andou reto (ambuláre's verb in 100:6) and the v2 Latinist's não prosperou (DRB), both options. Ps 101:29 semen eórum in sǽculum dirigétur → a sua descendência será dirigida para sempre — the stylist heard dirigida as administrative and asked guiada (refused: guiar is dedúcere's, D22; option).

Ps 106:38 multiplicáti sunt nimis → se multiplicaram sem medida (as 118:138, 78:8). confirmárePs 36 Ps 37 Ps 40 Ps 50 Ps 70 Ps 73 Ps 74 Ps 79 Ps 87 Ps 104 Ps 111 Ps 116 Ps 118confirmaropenPs 118:28 confirmai-me nas vossas palavras; options fortalecer (MS1932), firmar Ps 36:17 confírmat autem justos Dóminus → draft 2 mas o Senhor sustenta os justos: draft 1 confirma os justos was heard by the blind reader as 'reconhece ou atesta que eles são justos'. With persons as object confirmar is heard as attesting; sustentar (ὑποστηρίζει, 'props up'; free — sustinére is esperar por, D36) passed the Latinist. The Tuesday Matins antiphon Brácchia peccatórum * conteréntur, confírmat autem justos Dóminus follows. Proposal: confirmar only where a thing or a word is confirmed; with persons, sustentar (or firmar). Ps 37:3 and 37:20 confirmásti super me manum tuam … confirmáti sunt super me → firmastes sobre mim a vossa mão … se firmaram sobre mim — the row's option firmar, one verb for the psalm's echo (confirmastes a mão would be heard as attesting, as 36:17). The gate Latinist asked the passive foram fortalecidos (minor), refused for the echo; the blind reader heard 'gained the upper hand'. Evidence for a split: with a thing or a hand pressed upon someone → firmar. Ps 40:13 confirmásti me in conspéctu tuo → me firmastes na vossa presença — a person as object, the row's proposed firmar; passed the Latinist twice; the blind reader heard 'set me firmly before you'. Ps 50:14 e firmai-me com um espírito soberano (στήρισον): with a person as object confirmai-me is heard as the sacrament; firmar taken, passed the readers. Proposal: firmar whenever a person is the object. Ps 70:6 In te confirmátus sum → Em vós fui firmado (ἐπεστηρίχθην, the passive kept; MS1932 me firmei option); passed every reader. Ps 74:4 ego confirmávi colúmnas ejus → eu firmei as suas colunas — a thing set fast, the row's firmar (ἐστερέωσα); passed every reader. More evidence for firmar except where a word is confirmed. Ps 73:13 Tu confirmásti in virtúte tua mare → Vós firmastes o mar com o vosso poder — a thing made firm (ἐκραταίωσας); passed every reader. Ps 79:16 = 79:18 quem confirmásti tibi → que firmastes para vós — a person as object (ἐκραταίωσας σεαυτῷ), the row's firmar; passed the Latinist twice. fortalecestes option; MS1932 escolheste interprets. Ps 87:8 Super me confirmátus est furor tuus → Sobre mim se firmou o vosso furor (ἐπεστηρίχθη = 70:6); MS1932 and DM1962 pesou (the Hebrew) refused. No reader remarked. Ps 103:15 et panis cor hóminis confírmet → e que o pão fortaleça o coração do homem (στηρίζει; a heart as object): v1 sustente (after 36:17) was refused by the Latinist as feeding rather than strengthening; fortalecer (MS1932, DRB) passed the gate. firme the option. Evidence that with a heart as object fortalecer serves where firmar sounds odd. Ps 104:4 Quǽrite Dóminum, et confirmámini (κραταιώθητε) → Buscai o Senhor, e fortalecei-vos (MS1932 fortificai-vos): with a person as the subject of the passive imperative, confirmai-vos would be heard as the sacrament. firmai-vos, confirmai-vos are options (decision confirmamini). The same Greek verb is at 104:24 firmávit eum super → o fez mais forte que (the root kept). The colon is a Saturday Matins versicle and a Lenten Introit verse (formula row). Ps 111:7b confirmátum est cor ejus → o seu coração está firmado (ἐστήρικται = 70:6's verb): a heart set fast, not fed, so firmar rather than 103:15's fortalecer (option); passed both gates. Ps 116:2 Quóniam confirmáta est super nos misericórdia ejus → Porque se firmou sobre nós a sua misericórdia (ἐκραταιώθη; the build of 87:8 Sobre mim se firmou). The CNBB Liturgia das Horas has comprovado é seu amor (fetched, ps116/liturgy-br.txt) — the 'proved' hearing of confirmada printed in the official book, so the row's firmar holds. The v1 Latinist and the blind reader passed it (heard 'established upon us'); the v2 gate asked the passive foi confirmada (minor, voice), held; foi confirmada (MS1932, DRB) and foi firmada are options. Note 102:11 corroborávit (the same Greek) is fortaleceu: two Latin verbs, two Portuguese.

consíliumPs 1 Ps 9 Ps 12 Ps 13 Ps 19 Ps 20 Ps 30 Ps 32 Ps 65 Ps 70 Ps 82 Ps 110 Ps 118conselho (advice; a deliberating body; where a verse can mean both) / desígnio (what someone intends: 9:23, 19:5, 20:12, 32:10–11) — D33settled (D33)Ps 1:1 (Ps 118:24 already has it); open between advice and a deliberating body, as the Latin is — the blind reader heard both Ps 12:2 Até quando hei de pôr conselhos na minha alma — the stylist's hei de pôr (a deliberative future) for draft 1's porei; the blind reader heard advice kept first, deliberation second — the Latin's range; planos (MS1932 projectos) is an option. concíliumPs 1 Ps 21 Ps 25 Ps 39by its Greek (D34): congregação where συναγωγή (21:17); assembleia at 1:5 (βουλή, for the echo with 1:1 consílio); conselho at 25:4 (συνέδριον)settled (D34)Ps 1:5 in concílio justórum → na assembleia dos justos (from the stylist; DM1962's word). Draft 1 had the cognate concílio, for the Latin's echo consílio impiórum … concílio justórum (the Greek has βουλῇ twice): both blind readers stopped at it ("a council of bishops"; listed as unknown). Collision to rule on: assembleia is also the natural word for ecclésia, and Ps 21 has both (21:17 concílium malignántium, 21:23, 21:26 in ecclésia); other places 25:4, 39:11. congregação (MS1932) is congregátio's Ps 21 met the collision this row foretold, and rules it for review: two Latin words six verses apart, two Greek words (21:17 concílium malignántium = συναγωγὴ πονηρευομένων; 21:23, 21:26 ecclésia = ἐκκλησία), so two Portuguese words. ecclésia → assembleia everywhere (see the new row ecclésia); concílium here → a congregação dos malvados, on D15's test with synagóga → congregação (συναγωγή). The Greek behind concílium varies (read in the parallels files): 1:5 βουλή, 21:17 συναγωγή, 25:4 συνεδρίου, 39:11 συναγωγῆς. Proposal: concílium → congregação where it is συναγωγή (21:17, 39:11); 1:5 (βουλή) and 25:4 (συνέδριον) decide locally — 1:5's assembleia would then share the word with ecclésia in another psalm. Passed the Latinist twice; the blind reader heard 'a group of wicked people' (the cães as its image), never a religious order. Ps 25:4 Non sedi cum concílio vanitátis (συνεδρίου) → Não me sentei no conselho da vaidade — decided locally as D34 directs; draft 1 had com o conselho, and the blind reader heard advice (a recommendation dictated by vanity), so the preposition changed, not the word: one sits in a council. The gate Latinist (minor) wants com back for cum's company; refused, draft 1's words stay the option. Ps 39:11b a concílio multo → da congregação numerosa: checked — ἀπὸ συναγωγῆς πολλῆς (Rahlfs, in the parallels). D34's 'not yet checked' is closed. The stylist heard it 'administrative' and asked assembleia (ecclésia's, one verse before) — refused. multus → numerosa, not grande (magna, 39:10).

Ps 19:7a nunc cognóvi → agora soube (the Latinist: minor on agora sei on draft 1, MAJOR on the same words at the gate — the perfect of coming to know; saber que as 118:152). agora sei is option 2. Ps 73:5 non cognovérunt (no object) → não conheceram — v1 souberam (13:4's saber); the latinist and the stylist both asked for conhecer, which keeps the family with 73:9 não nos conhecerá mais. Ps 91:7 Vir insípiens non cognóscet (no object of its own) → não saberá, as 13:4; conhecerá (MS1932) option; no reader remarked.
fíeri, jussive FiatPs 33SejaopenPs 118:76, 80 (118:173 next): Faça-se (the glossary's fazer-se, and the Angelus') failed the stylist twice; DRB "let … be", MS1932 Seja; the row fíeri, factus est → fazer-se stands for the perfect 118:173 Fiat manus tua ut salvet me → Seja a vossa mão para me salvar: REFUSED BY THE STYLIST TWICE ("parece anunciar uma identificação que não chega"; he wants Que a vossa mão me venha salvar / Venha a vossa mão me salvar). Held, because his lines put veníre for fíeri and the build is that of 118:76, which he passed; the Latinist and the blind reader had nothing against it. For Gustavo's ear — option in decision fiat. Not for fíeri + predicate adjective: Ps 19:4 holocáustum tuum pingue fiat → o teu holocausto se torne gordo (the Latinist's MAJOR on seja: becoming, not a state; πιανάτω). See the row fíeri + adjective. Ps 40:14 fiat, fiat standing alone → assim seja, assim seja — see the formula row fiat, fiat. Ps 79:18 Fiat manus tua super virum déxteræ tuæ → Seja a vossa mão sobre o homem da vossa direita — as 118:173; the stylist called Seja … sobre a calque and asked Esteja (a state; held, option).

ego autem / ego veroPs 5 Ps 6 Ps 10 Ps 14 Ps 19 Ps 21 Ps 27 Ps 31 Ps 32 Ps 33 Ps 35 Ps 36 Ps 39 Ps 49 Ps 54 Ps 58 Ps 68 Ps 72 Ps 73 Ps 74 Ps 81 Ps 87 Ps 88 Ps 89 Ps 91 Ps 101 Ps 118mas eu / eu, porém,workingPs 118:69, 70, 78 — the Latin varies and so does the Portuguese Ps 16:15 Ego autem → Mas eu, as this row. dirígere at the vós imperativeendireitai (endireitai o meu caminho à vossa vista)openPs 5:9; dirigi is also "I directed" (D1/D13), and the enclitic does not save dírige me (24:5, 26:11: dirigi-me = "I made my way"). Endireitar is the verb's first sense (L&S "to lay straight, set in a straight line"), the Greek's (κατεύθυνον), and of the family of diréctio → retidão; safe (past endireitei). Places: 5:9, 89:16–17, 118:133; with me as object (24:5, 26:11) the psalm that meets it decides (encaminhai-me is a candidate). Options tornai reto; DM1962 aplainai is the Hebrew's image. No reader objected Ps 118:133 Gressus meos dírige → Endireitai os meus passos segundo o que dissestes: the row followed; no remark from any reader in eight readings. Cost there: the echo with 118:128 dirigébar (eu era dirigido) is not heard. Options Encaminhai (MS1932), Firmai (DM1962, the Hebrew's). Ps 24:5 Dírige me → Encaminhai-me (the row's candidate; safe, past encaminhei), and 24:9 Díriget → Encaminhará, so the psalm's one verb is heard twice. Passed the Latinist twice; no reader remarked. 26:11 should copy. Ps 26:11 dírige me in sémitam rectam → encaminhai-me à vereda reta — copied as the row directs; no remark. Ps 89:16–17 (×3) → encaminhai, departing from endireitai — endireitai os seus filhos is heard as correcting children; one verb for the Latin's three (encaminhai os seus filhos … encaminhai sobre nós as obras … e encaminhai a obra), though the Greek differs (ὁδήγησον / κατεύθυνον). The ambiguity reader heard 'guide' (and 'forward, as a document'). endireitai option. Proposes encaminhar where the object is persons or works; endireitar stays for ways and steps (5:9, 118:133). Note from Ps 95:10: endireitar now also renders corréxit (endireitou o mundo, readers' fault with corrigiu); weigh it when this row is ruled.
pérderePs 5 Ps 20 Ps 118fazer perecer (fareis perecer todos os que falam mentira)settled (D24)Ps 5:7a; the causative of períre → perecer, as ἀπόλλυμι is of ἀπόλλυμαι; keeps 72:27 períbunt: perdidísti as one figure and stays apart from dispérdere → exterminar, its neighbour in 142:12; 7 places (5:7a, 20:11, 25:9, 27:3, 33:17, 72:27, 142:12b), tried in each. The cognate perdereis (MS1932) is heard as "you will lose"; destruir (DRB) is banned at the vós imperative (destruí). No reader objected. Ps 118:95 ut pérderent me → para me fazer perecer — the same rendering, reached independently (118:92 has periíssem three verses before). The stylist found it "ceremonious and heavy" and drafts 8–10 had his para me destruir (safe as an infinitive); restored in draft 11 for this row's sake — if the row is ruled the other way, 118:95 returns to destruir in one touch Ps 20:11 Fructum eórum de terra perdes → Fareis perecer da terra o seu fruto. Ps 25:9 Ne perdas cum ímpiis, Deus, ánimam meam → Deus, não façais perecer com os ímpios a minha alma — the vocative moved first at the stylist's request; the Passiontide versicle stands alone. Ps 33:17 ut perdat de terra memóriam eórum → para fazer perecer da terra a memória deles — D24 followed at the place the row names. The stylist: «“Perecer da terra” não se acomoda à regência portuguesa» → fazer desaparecer; refused (D24), recorded. Passed the Latinist twice. Ps 72:27 períbunt: perdidísti → perecerão: fizestes perecer — applied as D24 names; the colon runs +6.
dolus / dolósus / dolóse ágerePs 5 Ps 7 Ps 9 Ps 11 Ps 12 Ps 16 Ps 17 Ps 23 Ps 34 Ps 35 Ps 37 Ps 40 Ps 47 Ps 49 Ps 51 Ps 54 Ps 68 Ps 72 Ps 119engano / enganador / enganar (o homem de sangue e enganador; com as suas línguas enganavam)openPs 5:7b, 5:11a; 19 verses (lábia dolósa 11:3–4, 16:1b, 30:18; lingua dolósa 51:6, 108:3, 119:2–3; dolos 34:20, 37:13, 49:19; dolóse egit 35:3). The cognate doloso is criminal law in Brazil. MS1932 has enganadores at 54:24. In 5:11a the light verb yields (the Greek has one verb, ἐδολιοῦσαν); agiam com engano is the option. 5:11a = 13:3b word for word as far as agébant: Ps 13 copies A sua garganta é um sepulcro aberto, † com as suas línguas enganavam Ps 11:3–4 lábia dolósa twice → lábios enganadores both times (one decision, two slots); in 11:3 com is supplied (com lábios enganadores) so that the lips are not heard as the subject of falaram. No reader remarked on the adjective. Ps 9:28 et dolo → e de engano: held; no critic remarked. Ps 14:3a qui non egit dolum in lingua sua → que não usou de engano com a sua língua (the noun kept; the light verb usar de, DRB's 'used deceit'; com for the instrumental in, from the stylist). Not the one verb enganar of 5:11a / 13:3b, because 14:4b has décipere (→ não engana; Greek ἀθετῶν) — a noun and a verb of one family for two Latin words. The stylist's praticou engano refused: praticar is operári's (14:2). 23:4 nec jurávit in dolo próximo suo (this psalm's cousin) → nem jurou com engano ao seu próximo. Ps 16:1b non in lábiis dolósis → que não é de lábios enganadores — the adjective held (a place this row named); the Latin's bare phrase given a relative and a copula (the blind reader and the stylist passed it; the Latinist passed it three times). não com lábios enganadores (11:3's com) is the option. Ps 23:4 applied, reordered: nem jurou ao seu próximo com engano — the pencilled com engano ao seu próximo would end the verse on the proparoxytone próximo (rule 4); heard as swearing falsely to deceive. Ps 33:14 ne loquántur dolum → e os teus lábios não falem engano (the stylist's com engano refused: the object is the thing said); the blind reader heard 'not tell lies'. Ps 31:2 nec est in spíritu ejus dolus → e em cujo espírito não há engano — applied. Ps 35:3 dolóse egit → agiu com engano (ágere kept, as 35:4 agir bem; enganou alone asks 'whom?'). Passed the Latinist twice. 35:4 dolus → engano. Ps 51:4 fecísti dolum → tramaste o engano: draft 1 fizeste engano (MS1932) was heard by the blind reader as 'you made a mistake' — engano after fazer is an error in daily speech; the verb gave way (decision dolum), losing the echo with 51:11 quia fecísti. Watch fazer engano elsewhere. Ps 51:6 lingua dolósa → língua enganadora (bare, vocative or apposition left open; ó the option). Ps 49:19 concinnábat dolos → tramava enganos (see concinnáre). Ps 72:18 propter dolos → por causa dos enganos — whose deceits left open, as the Latin. Ps 104:25 et dolum fácerent in servos ejus → e tramassem engano contra os seus servos (51:4's build for fácere dolum; decision dolum, with enganassem as the option for the one Greek verb δολιοῦσθαι). No reader remarked.
vir sánguinumPs 5 Ps 9 Ps 13 Ps 15 Ps 25 Ps 29 Ps 49 Ps 50 Ps 54 Ps 78 Ps 105homem de sangueopenPs 5:7b (DM1962's words); the Hebraism kept concrete, the plural lost (as in DRB); 25:9, 54:24 Viri sánguinum, et dolósi (→ Os homens de sangue e enganadores), 138:19; MS1932 sanguinário everywhere Ps 15:4b conventícula eórum de sanguínibus → os seus ajuntamentos de sangue: the plural lost as in this row, HELD against a Latinist major twice (he wants de sangues). The blind reader heard 'reuniões com derramamento de sangue' first, 'ritos com sangue' second — both readings of the plural. See the new open row sanguínes (plural). Ps 54:24b applied as foreseen: Os homens de sangue e enganadores; the stylist's e os enganadores (two groups) is an option (decision viri); the blind reader heard violent men.
multitúdo (+ genitive)Ps 5 Ps 9 Ps 32 Ps 36 Ps 43 Ps 50 Ps 65 Ps 76multidão (na multidão da vossa misericórdia; segundo a multidão das suas impiedades)openPs 5:7b, 5:11b — the psalm sets the two against each other, so one word; 17 verses (50:3b secúndum multitúdinem miseratiónum tuárum; 68:14 = 5:7b's phrase; 36:11 in multitúdine pacis; 146:4 multitúdinem stellárum). Abundância (MS1932 in 5:8) is abundántia's (29:7, 71:7 abundántia pacis), grandeza magnitúdo's (150:2 has both). Odd with a singular abstract, as the Latin is; no reader stumbled on it — the blind reader heard "because they are many" before "in proportion to" at 5:11b Ps 30:20 Quam magna multitúdo dulcédinis tuæ → Como é grande, Senhor, a multidão da vossa doçura: the blind reader heard people first ('multidão' suggests a crowd), quantity at once after. Ps 36:11 in multitúdine pacis → na multidão da paz: the stylist asked numa multidão de paz (heard as a crowd); the blind reader heard 'abundância de paz' first, a crowd second. Kept; passed the Latinist twice. Ps 43:13 e não houve multidão nas trocas deles: the Latin's openness (a great sum, or a crowd of buyers) kept; the blind reader found no clear meaning; options abundância, concorrência (MS1932). Ps 51:9 in multitúdine divitiárum suárum = 48:7 → na multidão das suas riquezas; the stylist asked abundância (refused: abundántia's), the blind reader heard a crowd second. Ps 63:3 a multitúdine operántium iniquitátem → da multidão dos que praticam a iniquidade. Ps 65:3 In multitúdine virtútis tuæ → na multidão do vosso poder — the ambiguity reader heard 'in the crowd' once; kept. Ps 76:18 Multitúdo sónitus aquárum (verbless) → Grande estrondo das águas (v2): A multidão do estrondo is heard as a crowd; draft 1 Muito estrondo was colloquial to the stylist; the v2 Latinist (minor) asked Multidão do som — held, option. Of a mass noun the multitude is its greatness.

irritárePs 5 Ps 9 Ps 73 Ps 105 Ps 106provocar (porque vos provocaram, Senhor)settled (D27)Ps 5:11b; 10 verses (9:34, 73:10, 105:7, 16, 29, 32, 106:11; the noun in 94:8 in irritatióne → provocação); L&S quote Nonius: inritare dictum est proprie provocare; DRB provoked; irritar (MS1932) has sunk to "annoy". árguererepreender (não me repreendais no vosso furor)settled (D21)D21 overrules the agent’s acusar (kept as an option in Ps 6): every living witness says rebuke, and acusar makes God the prosecutor. The word is shared with increpáre; they never meet in a verse. The agent’s note: Ps 6:2 = 37:2; 5 verses (6:2, 37:2, 49:8, 49:21 árguam te, et státuam contra fáciem tuam, 93:10). L&S: with a person, "to accuse, reprove, censure, charge with" (arguisse accusasse et convicisse, Dig.); ἐλέγχω. Repreender (DRB rebuke, DM1962) is what the ear expects but is increpáre's word (ἐπιτιμάω, 12 verses), and repreendais has a hiatus at the stress; accusáre does not occur in the psalter; MS1932 arguir is an examiner's verb in Brazil. No reader objected. Gustavo's ear wanted: it opens two Penitential Psalms Ps 49:8 Non in sacrifíciis tuis árguam te → Não te repreenderei pelos teus sacrifícios; 49:21 árguam te → eu te repreenderei.
corríperecastigar (nem me castigueis na vossa ira)settled (D21)Ps 6:2 = 37:2; 7 verses (38:12, 89:10, 93:10 Qui córripit gentes, non árguet?, 104:14, 140:5 Corrípiet me justus in misericórdia, et increpábit me). Shares the word with castigáre (117:18) on D15's test: one Greek verb (παιδεύω — checked for 117:18 in the parallels) and the two never meet (castigáre has no other verse). Corrigir is corrígere's (17:36b, 95:10, 118:9). MS1932, DRB chastise Ps 38:12 corripuísti hóminem → castigastes o homem, as this row names. Ps 89:10b et corripiémur → e seremos castigados — applied. Ps 95:10 corréxit → endireitou, not corrigiu — the v1 stylist heard corrigiu o mundo as grading homework and the ambiguity reader as 'corrected / punished'; endireitar is L&S's first sense ('to make straight') and the Greek's (κατώρθωσεν), and keeps the moral sense in Portuguese. The v2 Latinist passed it. Cost: endireitai is the open imperative of dirígere (D22) — another form, and the two do not meet here. corrigiu option. So corrígere now has corrigir (17:36b) and endireitar (95:10).

Masculine in the Latin too Ps 102:3 infirmitátes → enfermidades, as the row foresaw.
