Ps 59:4 sana → curai — applied; no remark. Ps 102:3 qui sanat omnes infirmitátes tuas → que cura todas as tuas enfermidades.
valde / veheménterPs 6 Ps 20 Ps 30 Ps 46 Ps 47 Ps 77 Ps 103 Ps 118muito (both)openPs 6:4, 6:11. Draft 1 kept them apart (grandemente); the stylist found it heavy. Merged on D15's test — σφόδρα all three times in this psalm — and it lets 6:11 muito perturbados answer 6:4 muito perturbada. veheménter elsewhere (20:2, 46:10, 103:1, 104:24, 118:140, 167) may want grandemente locally Ps 118:167 diléxit ea veheménter → e os amou muito (held; short by three syllables). 118:140 Ignítum … veheménter → está todo em brasa: muito em brasa is not said; the Latinist (draft 16, minor) notes that todo is totality, not intensity — refused as the idiomatic intensive. Ps 20:2 exsultábit veheménter → exultará muito. Ps 30:12 et vicínis meis valde → e sobremaneira para os meus vizinhos — a local departure. Draft 1 e muito para os meus vizinhos was the stylist's worst line (muito hangs, not tied to afronta) and the blind reader could hear 'many neighbours'; draft 2 sobretudo (MS1932) was marked MAJOR by the Latinist gate (a comparison the Latin does not make) and his sobremaneira was taken verbatim (draft 3, unread). Where valde bears on a dative or stands at the end of a member, muito may need this help; grandemente is the option. Ps 30:12 → grandemente (Ps 30 draft 4, review 2026-09-21): sobremaneira (draft 3, the Latinist’s gate verbatim) was unknown to the blind reader; muito had been heard as “many neighbours”. A local departure from muito, as before. Ps 46:10 veheménter eleváti sunt → foram muito elevados (the stylist's sobremaneira refused, as at 30:12; grandemente option).
úsquequoPs 4 Ps 12 Ps 81 Ps 88 Ps 118até quandoworkingPs 4:3, Ps 6:4 mas vós, Senhor, até quando? — the broken question left broken; 10 verses Ps 12:1–3: four Até quando — Úsquequo ×3 and 12:2 Quámdiu, merged (the Latin's anaphora is the psalm's shape; the stylist praised the repeated Até quando; Por quanto tempo for quámdiu is option 2). quámdiu elsewhere is "as long as" (103:33 quámdiu sum, 145:2a quámdiu fúero) and decides there. Ps 93:3 twice, Até quando os pecadores, Senhor, * até quando os pecadores se gloriarão?
inférnus / ínferiPs 6 Ps 9 Ps 13 Ps 15 Ps 17 Ps 29 Ps 30 Ps 48 Ps 54 Ps 62 Ps 85 Ps 87 Ps 93 Ps 105 Ps 113 Ps 114infernoopenPs 6:6 no inferno, porém, quem vos dará graças? — the Latin's word, kept (DRB hell). The blind reader heard the hell of the damned first, the world of the dead second. In 6:6 both are true; the hard tests are 15:10 non derelínques ánimam meam in inférno and 138:8 si descéndero in inférnum, ades; 19 verses. Options: os infernos (the old plural for the abode of the dead — the Creed's wording, from memory, unverified), a mansão dos mortos (the Creed as now said in Brazil — unverified; a paraphrase), MS1932 habitação dos mortos, DM1962 limbos. Heavy: wants a ruling Ps 9:18 Convertántur peccatóres in inférnum → Voltem os pecadores para o inferno: kept; here the damned's hell is no mishearing — the verse is a curse on the wicked; none of the three critics stopped at it. Ps 17:6 As dores do inferno me cercaram: kept (DRB the sorrows of hell); the blind reader heard the torments of the damned first, as foreseen — here the parallel laços da morte in the same verse points to the realm of the dead. For Gustavo with the rest of the row. Ps 15:10 — the hard test this row named: Quóniam non derelínques ánimam meam in inférno → Porque não abandonareis a minha alma no inferno: kept (DRB hell; MS1932 here no inferno). The Clementine of Acts, fetched (consult/bolls-VULG-44-2.json, -44-13.json), quotes the colon word for word (Acts 2:27) and applies it to Christ in 2:31 neque derelictus est in inferno, neque caro ejus vidit corruptionem; 13:35 quotes 15:10b. The blind reader heard, as foreseen, the place of punishment first, the realm of the dead second; the Latinist passed it twice; no critic asked for a change. Options in Ps 15: nos infernos, na mansão dos mortos, na morada dos mortos (the Creed's wordings still unverified). With 6:6, 9:18, 17:6 the row now has its four tests — ready for Gustavo's ruling. Ps 29:4 eduxísti ab inférno ánimam meam → tirastes do inferno a minha alma: kept (DRB hell; MS1932 inferno with a note, 'the grave'). The blind reader heard 'the place of eternal damnation' first, the world of the dead second — the fourth place so heard (after 6:6, 17:6, 15:10); here, as in 15:10, it is a soul brought back from it, where the damned's hell is the wrong sense. Passed the Latinist twice. mundo dos mortos is the option in Ps 29. Ps 30:18 deducántur in inférnum → sejam conduzidos ao inferno — a curse on the wicked, as 9:18; no reader stopped at it. dedúci in → ser conduzido (the passive of dúcere; D25's fazer descer has no sayable passive). Ps 48:15, 15b, 16 (three places): Como ovelhas foram postos no inferno; envelhecerá no inferno; da mão do inferno — the wicked's fate twice, the psalmist rescued from it once (as 29:4); the blind reader heard damnation first, as foreseen. Ps 85:13 ex inférno inferióri → do inferno mais profundo (v1 mais baixo; mais profundo the stylist's). The ambiguity reader again heard the hell of the damned first; kept, the Latin's word. Ps 87:4 et vita mea inférno appropinquávit → e a minha vida se aproximou do inferno — kept; the ambiguity reader heard the hell of the damned first, as foreseen (the realm of the dead is meant, as 29:4). Ps 93:17 por pouco teria habitado no inferno a minha alma — the ambiguity reader heard hell; kept (the Latin's word). Ps 114:3a perícula inférni → os perigos do inferno (= 17:6's dores do inferno; parallel to dores da morte); the ambiguity reader heard the hell of the damned first again. Kept; abismo and mundo dos mortos options. Ps 113:25 neque omnes, qui descéndunt in inférnum → nem todos os que descem ao inferno — the ambiguity reader again heard the hell of the damned; kept.

Which contexts take which tense: odi / odívi, odérunt, odísti are perfects of a state and take the present (24:19, 25:5, 30:7, 118:104); ódio hábui keeps the past periphrasis (118:113, 128) or Odiei (118:163); a past narrative keeps the past (35:5 malítiam autem non odívit → não odiou a malícia, beside meditátus est … ástitit). Ps 100:3 odívi in a narrative of imperfects → odiei (the perfect's past: DRB 'I hated', ἐμίσησα), not the present sense of 25:5 / 118:104; odiava, odeio options. Context decides.

dissipárePs 17 Ps 32 Ps 34 Ps 52 Ps 118dissiparopenPs 118:126 dissiparam a vossa lei; heard by the blind reader as "made the law disappear / destroyed it"; options desfazer, DM1962 violar (the Hebrew's); 9 verses (17:15, 32:10, 34:16, 52:6, 67:2, 67:31b, 140:8, 143:6) Ps 17:15 dissipávit eos (people) → e os dispersou: dissipou was unknown to the blind reader and heard as translated by the stylist. elóquium — evidence from 118:81–128 for whoever reviews D16Ps 11 Ps 17 Ps 18 Ps 103 Ps 104 Ps 106 Ps 118clause kept (118:82, 116); plural os vossos ditos kept (118:103); noun o dito da vossa justiça (118:123)openThe clause passed the stylist twice and the blind reader; the Latinist, on his third reading only, marked its past tense minor (118:82, 116) — D16's named cost. The plural ditos, which had passed every reader at 118:11, was refused by the stylist twice at 118:103 ("maxims, popular sayings … a translator's choice"). The noun at 118:123 was refused by him twice and understood at once by the blind reader. Alternatives for the main session: (a) stand; (b) D16's retreat, palavra, for the whole term (one touch: label palavras of decision eloquia in Ps 118); (c) the clause at 118:123 too — à espera do que disse a vossa justiça (option in decision v123b; it makes justice the speaker) EVIDENCE FROM 118:129–176 (nine places; four Latinist, two stylist and two blind readings, ps118/critic/v13–v16.*.part4.json). SINGULAR, the clause, six places, none of which forced a noun: 118:133 segundo o que dissestes · 118:140 O que dissestes está todo em brasa … o amou (the clause as SUBJECT, with a predicate and a pronoun pointing back) · 118:154 pelo que dissestes vivificai-me (after propter: cause is what the Latin says, so the hearing the handoff feared is here the right one) · 118:169 conforme o que dissestes · 118:170 segundo o que dissestes libertai-me · 118:172 pronunciará o que dissestes. Stylist: no remark against the clause in any of the six places on either reading; on the first reading his own lines for 118:154 and 118:169 keep it; on the second his line for 118:154 reads pela vossa palavra, though the faults he named there were an echo and a rhyme. Blind reader: understood every place, twice (118:169 → como prometestes); nothing misheard after a preposition. Latinist: six minors on draft 13 and again on draft 14, all one remark — the clause dates an utterance the noun leaves timeless (D16's named cost); then NO remark on drafts 15 and 16 with the clause unchanged. PLURAL os vossos ditos, three places (118:148 meditar nos vossos ditos, 118:158 não guardaram os vossos ditos, 118:162 alegrarei com os vossos ditos): refused by the stylist in all three, on both readings — six of six ("máximas ou frases célebres", "uma coleção de máximas", "coloração de máxima ou anedota", "deixam aparecer o tradutor"), each time for palavras; the blind reader understood it (118:158 → Não obedeceram ao que Deus disse) and never listed ditos as unknown; the Latinist never remarked on it. So over the whole psalm the verdicts have converged: the clause has held with the ear everywhere since D16 (stylist and blind reader), at the price of a recurring Latinist minor; the plural noun is what the stylist refuses — 118:11 passed, then 118:103 twice, 118:148, 158, 162 twice each. Alternatives for Gustavo: (a) stand; (b) palavra(s) for the whole term (one touch per psalm: label palavras of decision eloquia) — costs λόγιον / λόγος, and makes secúndum elóquium tuum = secúndum verbum tuum; (c) a split nobody has tried: keep the clause for the singular (15 of 20) and give only the plural (5 of 20: 118:11, 103, 148, 158, 162) to palavras — the ear's verdicts exactly, at the cost of one Latin noun having a clause and a borrowed noun. Ruled in D26: a fourth way, the clause in both numbers.
redímerePs 25 Ps 48 Ps 106 Ps 118resgatar (enquanto não há quem resgate, nem quem salve)openPs 7:3; λυτρόομαι; 12 verses with the present stem (grep: 7:3, 25:11, 33:23, 43:26, 48:8, 48:16, 54:19, 71:14, 102:4, 118:134, 118:154, 129:8) and 9 with the perfect (30:6 redemísti me, Dómine, Deus veritátis — the verse of In manus tuas; 70:23, 73:2, 76:15, 77:42, 105:10, 106:2, 135:24, 143:10): resgatastes-me must be weighed there against remir (vós me remistes — the traditional verb, from memory, unverified). The cognate fails at the four imperatives: redimi-me is also "I redeemed myself" (D13's test) — resgatai-me, resgatai-nos are safe. The noun redémptio (110:9a, 129:7) can stay redenção. MS1932 livrar is liberáre's Ps 118:134, 154 reached the same verb independently: Resgatai-me das calúnias dos homens; Julgai em juízo a minha causa, e resgatai-me — for the reason this row gives (Redimi-me / Remi-me are also "I redeemed myself"; rule 3). The Diurnal has the verb at 118:134. Passed the Latinist four times, the stylist and the blind reader twice each, with no remark. In 118:154 it rhymes with vivificai-me at the cadence — the Latin's own echo (rédime me … vivífica me), accepted. Ps 25:11 rédime me → resgatai-me — applied (safe: past resgatei). Ps 30:6 redemísti me, Dómine, Deus veritátis → vós me resgatastes, Senhor, Deus da verdade — weighed against remistes, as this row asked: remir is safe in the perfect and is the Redeemer's verb, but the imperatives cannot take it (remi-me), so it would split one Latin verb (λυτρόομαι) in two. Serves the Compline responsory's versicle Redemísti nos (Vós nos resgatastes). Passed the Latinist twice; remistes is the option (decision redemisti). Ps 33:23 Rédimet Dóminus ánimas servórum suórum → O Senhor resgatará as almas dos seus servos; the blind reader heard salvation after death first, rescue from danger second — the Latin's range. Ps 48:8 Frater non rédimit, rédimet homo → O irmão não resgata, o homem resgatará (the Latin as punctuated: no question, no second non; MS1932's question and DRB's nor are options); 48:16 Deus rédimet ánimam meam → Deus resgatará a minha alma; the noun 48:9 prétium redemptiónis → o preço do resgate, to keep the psalm's one root (the redémptio note's redenção is the option there). Passed the Latinist twice. Ps 70:23 quam redemísti → que resgatastes. Ps 76:15 redemísti in brácchio tuo → resgatastes com o vosso braço — applied (as 30:6). Ps 102:4 Qui rédimit → Que resgata. Ps 106:2 qui redémpti sunt … quos redémit → os resgatados … os que ele resgatou — the row applied; remidos … remiu option.

Antecipar is left to anticipáre (76:5 Anticipavérunt vigílias óculi mei, 78:8). Not settled: the transitive use with a person — 16:13 prǽveni eum, 17:19, 20:4 prævenísti eum in benedictiónibus, 58:10 misericórdia ejus prævéniet me, 87:14 orátio mea prævéniet te; also 67:26, 67:31b (nine verses with the stem, by grep) — which will want vir ao encontro de or the like Ps 17:19 transitive and hostile: Prævenérunt me in die afflictiónis meæ → Surpreenderam-me, one verb with 17:6 præoccupavérunt me láquei mortis → me surpreenderam — one Greek verb (προέφθασάν με) in both, D15's test. The Latinist (minor) wanted Anteciparam-se a mim; refused. The friendly transitive places (20:4, 58:10, 87:14) are not settled by this. Ps 16:13 prǽveni eum (God the subject, the enemy the object; πρόφθασον) → adiantai-vos a ele: draft 1 had 17:19's surpreendei-o (the same Greek verb); the Latinist marked it MAJOR — «pede antecipação: chegar antes dele ou adiantar-se a ele» — and asked for antecipai-vos a ele. Taken with this row's own verb (antecipar is anticipáre's). So with a person as object: hostile to the speaker surpreender (17:19), God forestalling the enemy adiantar-se a (16:13). The friendly places (20:4, 58:10, 87:14) are still open. Transitive, God forestalling with good: Ps 20:4 prævenísti eum in benedictiónibus dulcédinis → vos adiantastes a ele com bênçãos de doçura (the Latinist's minor on draft 1's viestes ao encontro dele: the anticipation; his antecipar is anticipáre's). Agrees with 16:13 adiantai-vos a ele; hostile prævenire keeps surpreender (17:19). Ps 58:10 misericórdia ejus prævéniet me → a sua misericórdia se adiantará a mim (friendly, the family of 16:13, 20:4 kept). The stylist found it bureaucratic, the final a mim limp, and asked me precederá; the ambiguity reader heard 'go ahead of me' and also 'overtake'. Held; me precederá is option 2 of decision praeveniet — the friendly places are still open, and 87:14 orátio mea prævéniet te will test it again. Ps 76:5 Anticipavérunt vigílias óculi mei → Os meus olhos anteciparam as vigílias — the cognate this row reserved; se adiantaram às (MS1932) the option. The ambiguity reader found the line obscure and vigílias unknown / heard as church vigils. Draft 1 had the row's se adiantará a vós; the stylist called it unidiomatic (the second stylist to refuse it, after 58:10) and the ambiguity reader heard 'outrun you'. Proposed: friendly transitive → preceder (58:10 me precederá should follow; 20:4 decides); hostile surpreender (17:19) and 16:13 adiantai-vos a ele untouched. Cost: præcédere (96:3) will need another word. The R. of the Sunday Prime preces reads alone. Passed the v2 Latinist. Ps 83:10, decided locally as this row asked: áspice (ἴδε) → vede, réspice in (ἐπίβλεψον) → olhai para (Deus, nosso protetor, vede: * e olhai para a face do vosso Cristo). The Greek splits the pair; ἐπίβλεψον is the verb 118:132 and 12:3 render olhai, so réspice keeps the rows' verb and áspice here takes ver. Passed the Latinist twice. The colon is the Preces versicle and the Introit of Pentecost XIV. Ps 89:16 Réspice in servos tuos, et in ópera tua → Olhai para os vossos servos e para as vossas obras — the imperative formula. Ps 112:5 et humília réspicit → e olha para as coisas humildes — olhar para, as 103:32, 30:8, 32:14. justítiæ (plural)Ps 5 Ps 7 Ps 9 Ps 10 Ps 17 Ps 22 Ps 30 Ps 36 Ps 47 Ps 49 Ps 50 Ps 57 Ps 70 Ps 71 Ps 74 Ps 88 Ps 93 Ps 98 Ps 102 Ps 105 Ps 117 Ps 118as justiças (e amou as justiças)openPs 10:8, where the Greek is δικαιοσύνας (plural of δικαιοσύνη); DRB and MS1932 make it singular. Ps 18:9 Justítiæ Dómini rectæ → As justiças do Senhor são retas — the Latin's plural kept though the Greek here is δικαιώματα (not δικαιοσύνας as at 10:8); heard as 'the acts by which the Lord does justice', norms second. Ps 88:32 Si justítias meas profanáverint (δικαιώματα) → Se profanarem as minhas justiças — the row kept while it is open. Ps 44:7 Sedes tua, Deus → O teu trono, ó Deus (the king addressed as God). Ps 92:2 Paráta sedes tua ex tunc → O vosso trono está preparado desde então — no reader objected to trono. inops / pauper / egénusPs 9 Ps 10 Ps 11 Ps 21 Ps 24 Ps 30 Ps 34 Ps 36 Ps 40 Ps 48 Ps 68 Ps 71 Ps 78 Ps 81 Ps 106 Ps 111 Ps 112carente / pobre / (necessitado)settled (D38)Ps 11:6a Por causa da miséria dos indigentes, e do gemido dos pobres. The Latin keeps three words (and mendícus, 39:18, 108:17) and pairs them constantly: inops 14 lines (13:6, 34:10, 36:14, 71:13, 73:21 pauper et inops, 85:1 inops, et pauper sum ego, 108:17, 112:7, 139:13 …), egénus 6 (34:10, 40:2, 69:6, 81:3–4, 108:22 — grep). Proposed: pauper → pobre; inops ("without means") → indigente, whose noun indigência serves inópia (33:10, 43:24, 87:9, 106:41); egénus → necessitado, reserved. The blind reader listed indigentes as unknown twice; options desvalidos (MS1932), necessitados. The stylist named 11:6a the psalm's best line Ps 9 (stage one + two): pauper → pobre in 12 places (9:10, 13, 19 ×2, 23, 30a, 30b ×2, 31, 33, 35b, 38); húmilis 9:39 → humilde (the blind reader heard 'poor and simple', beside órfão) — proposed as the fourth member: húmilis → humilde, humílitas → humilhação (9:14). D27: húmilis → humilde settled beside pauper → pobre; inops stays open (indigente was unknown to the blind reader twice). Ps 13:6 consílium ínopis → o conselho do indigente, kept under this row: listed as unknown by the blind reader for the third time (Ps 11 twice, Ps 13 once). Heard otherwise rightly (the next colon's a sua esperança taken as his). The evidence against indigente is now three readings of three; if it is to change, desvalido (MS1932 in Ps 11) is the candidate that keeps pobre for pauper. egére (the verb), Ps 15:2 (DO 15:1) quóniam bonórum meórum non eges → porque não precisais dos meus bens — the plain verb; não tendes necessidade (MS1932, the link to necessitado) is the option. Only place (grep). Ps 33:10 quóniam non est inópia timéntibus eum → draft 2 porque nada falta aos que o temem: draft 1's não há indigência (this row's proposal) was unknown to the blind reader and 'administrative' to the stylist; the noun turned into the verb faltar (Douay-Rheims 'there is no want to them that fear him'). indigência is option 2 in Ps 33's decision inopia. Evidence against indigência for inópia (43:24, 87:9, 106:41 still to come): the noun fared no better than the adjective. 33:7 Iste pauper → Este pobre (the blind reader heard the speaker himself). 33:11 Dívites eguérunt → Os ricos passaram necessidade e fome, egére kept apart from inópia. Ps 34:10b — all three in one verse: Erípiens ínopem … egénum et páuperem → Vós que arrancais o carente … o necessitado e o pobre. Draft 1 tried desvalido (Matos Soares 1932): unknown to the blind reader, like indigente before it. Draft 2 carente passed the Latinist. Proposal for the row: inops → carente (known, and apart from pobre and necessitado); indigente has now failed three blind readers and desvalido one. Ps 36:14b páuperem et ínopem → o pobre e o indigente: unknown to the blind reader for the FOURTH time in four readings (Pss 11 ×2, 13, 36). Kept on the row so the evidence stays in one place. Proposal for a ruling: inops → desvalido psalter-wide (MS1932 in Ps 11; keeps pobre for pauper and the pair's two words). D38 (review 2026-09-21): inops → carente in all four finished places — 11:6a dos carentes, 13:6 do carente, 34:10b, 36:14b o pobre e o carente (Pss 11 draft 3, 13 draft 3, 36 draft 5). Indigente was unknown to four blind readers of four; desvalido to one. Both stay options in each psalm. inópia (33:10, 43:24, 87:9, 106:41) is not ruled by D38. Ps 40:2 super egénum, et páuperem → acerca do necessitado e do pobre — egénus → necessitado beside pobre, as 34:10b; no reader stopped at either word. Ps 71:13 páuperi et ínopi → o pobre e o carente (D38); the stylist asked necessitado ('social-work vocabulary') — refused: egénus's word. Ps 81:3–4 egénus twice → necessitado (as 69:6), pauper → pobre, húmilis → humilde; no remark from any reader. Ps 85:1 quóniam inops, et pauper sum ego → porque eu sou carente e pobre (the ruling). Evidence against it: the stylist (necessitado e pobre, refused under D38) and the ambiguity reader both heard carente as emotional neediness first; the ambiguity reader listed its material sense as unknown. Two readers in one psalm — worth Gustavo's look at D38. Ps 108:17 hóminem ínopem, et mendícum → o homem carente, e mendigo; 108:22 egénus, et pauper → necessitado e pobre; 108:31 páuperis → do pobre. The stylist heard carente as emotional need and asked indigente — refused, D38. Ps 112:7 Súscitans a terra ínopem → o carente (D38) — the stylist heard social-work / emotional 'uma pessoa carente' and asked necessitado; the ambiguity reader named the emotional sense second. Kept under D38; more evidence for the fault already noted at 85:1, 87:9.

The noun humílitas → humilhação and the verb humiliáre → humilhar are the row humílitas / humiliáre (open; 21:22 a minha pequenez).

castusPs 11 Ps 26 Ps 72 Ps 117puro (palavras puras)openPs 11:7 only (grep); ἁγνός. castas was heard by the blind reader as sexual chastity and listed as unknown; puro meets mundus (50:12 cor mundum) in no verse. MS1932 sinceras is sincérus's
examináre / probárePs 11 Ps 16 Ps 17 Ps 25 Ps 65examinar / provar (prata examinada no fogo, provada, purificada da terra sete vezes)openPs 11:7; 65:10 sets them side by side (probásti nos, Deus: igne nos examinásti, sicut examinátur argéntum), so two verbs; provar also 16:3, 25:2, 138:23 Proba me. L&S examino "to weigh, test". provada no fogo is the idiom but would give provar to examináre. 17:31 igne examináta follows. terræ left where it can hang on either participle (DRB purged from the earth; MS1932's no crisol interprets) Ps 17:31 elóquia Dómini igne examináta → as palavras do Senhor, examinadas no fogo (D27), verbless as the Latin; the blind reader heard 'put to the test and proved true'. Passed the Latinist. Ps 16:3 sets the two in one verse (Probásti cor meum … igne me examinásti) → Provastes o meu coração … no fogo me examinastes — two verbs kept two, as this row wanted (65:10 next); no fogo as 11:7, 17:31. Passed every reader. Ps 25:2 Proba me, Dómine, et tenta me → Provai-me, Senhor, e experimentai-me — see the new row tentáre. Ps 65:10 probásti nos … igne nos examinásti, sicut examinátur argéntum → nos provastes … no fogo nos examinastes, como se examina a prata — the two verbs kept two; the ambiguity reader noted provar 'taste', carried by the fire and silver.
fiduciáliter (ágere)Ps 11com confiança (nele agirei com confiança)openPs 11:6b only (L&S cite it); παρρησιάσομαι. nele as open as in eo. The blind reader heard the colon as the psalmist's, twice — the Latin marks the Lord's words off no better. MS1932 confiadamente
diminúere, diminútæ suntdiminuir, intransitive (diminuíram as verdades)openPs 11:2 only; ὠλιγώθησαν "became few"; the intransitive for a medio-passive, as se elevou (8:2b). The Latinist passed it on draft 1 and marked the voice on draft 2, words unchanged; foram diminuídas and minguaram are options
altitúdoPs 11 Ps 55 Ps 68altura (segundo a vossa altura)openPs 11:9 (of God); 55:4, 68:3 altitúdinem maris, 94:4 altitúdines móntium, 102:11 secúndum altitúdinem cæli (grep) — the concrete word everywhere; alteza is a royal title; the blind reader heard "greatness" first Ps 55:4 Ab altitúdine diéi timébo → Da altura do dia temerei — the concrete word kept at the crux (noon, or height as pride); the Latinist (v1) asked plain da for draft 1's desde, which made ab only temporal. MS1932 desde que desponta o dia refused. The blind reader listed altura do dia as unclear — the Latin's own obscurity. Ps 68:3b Veni in altitúdinem maris → Cheguei ao alto-mar (MS1932) — à altura do mar is heard as a position. The gate Latinist (minor) asked à profundeza do mar (the Greek's βάθη); held: it would merge with profúndum → profundeza (68:3, 68:16). Option. Ps 94:4 altitúdines móntium → as alturas dos montes — heard as the peaks; no remark. Ps 102:11 secúndum altitúdinem cæli a terra → segundo a altura do céu acima da terra — the concrete word; the ambiguity reader heard a vague 'according to', and the comparison may not come through (the Latin's own build).
in circúituPs 17 Ps 26 Ps 30 Ps 33 Ps 96ao redor (de)workingPs 11:9 Os ímpios andam ao redor (no de nós, which MS1932 adds); 15 lines (grep), most with a genitive: 33:8, 49:3, 88:9 véritas tua in circúitu tuo, 124:2b, 127:3b in circúitu mensæ tuæ Ps 33:8 Immíttet Ángelus Dómini in circúitu timéntium eum → O anjo do Senhor acampará ao redor dos que o temem (κύκλῳ). Ps 75:12 in circúitu ejus → ao seu redor (the stylist's possessive form, draft 2), placed before the verb so it is not heard as 'bring gifts around him'. Ps 96:2 in circúitu ejus → ao seu redor (75:12's form); 96:3 inflammábit in circúitu → queimará ao redor (no object, as 11:9).
próximusPs 11 Ps 14 Ps 21 Ps 23 Ps 27 Ps 34 Ps 37 Ps 44 Ps 87próximoworkingPs 11:3; a proparoxytone: at a cadence it needs a word after it (11:3 was recast so that the mediant falls on coisas vãs); 14:3b, 14:4b, 23:4, 27:3, 34:14, 37:12 (grep) Ps 14:3b Nec fecit próximo suo malum → nem fez ao seu próximo o mal (the Latin's order, so that the mediant falls on mal; the stylist's fez mal ao seu próximo is the option, refused under rule 4) and e contra os seus próximos não aceitou afronta (the phrase fronted so that the verse does not end on próximos). 14:4b jura ao seu próximo (not at a cadence). Ps 27:3b Qui loquúntur pacem cum próximo suo → Os que com o seu próximo falam de paz — the proparoxytone kept off the cadence, as the row asks. Ps 34:14 Quasi próximum → como a um próximo, off the cadence (draft 2 puts the sic clause first). *Ps 37:12 *Amíci mei, et próximi mei ** → *Os meus amigos e os meus próximos ** — the one place where the proparoxytone stands at the mediant: draft 1's postposed *Os amigos meus e os próximos meus (to save the cadence) was refused by the stylist as calqued and precious; the plain order won (D2: the ear leads on order). His vizinhos refused (vicínus's; and próximos … aproximaram echoes próximi … appropinquavérunt). Ps 44:15b próximæ ejus (αἱ πλησίον, the bride's companions) → as que lhe são próximas (the root kept; MS1932 companheiras would merge with 44:8 consórtes).

séptuplumPs 11 Ps 78sete vezesworkingPs 11:7 (DRB, MS1932); 78:12 redde … séptuplum is a noun (sete vezes mais) and decides there
oblivísci, obliviscéris (12:1)Ps 12esquecer (me esquecereis)openPs 12:1 — the future, by the accent: obliviscéris (long ē) against the present 43:24 oblivísceris (Greek ἐπιλήσῃ, future). The accent in the psalter text is the evidence to cite whenever a 3rd-conjugation -eris comes up Ps 41:10 Quare oblítus es mei? → Por que me esquecestes? (genitive object → direct).
obdormírePs 12adormecer (para que eu nunca adormeça na morte)openPs 12:4b; 43:23 quare obdórmis, Dómine? (of God) is the only other (grep) and should follow (por que adormeceis); the blind reader heard "so that I do not die" first; dormir is dormíre's (3:6, 4:9) Ps 43:23 por que adormeceis, Senhor? — applied; no reader remarked.
movéri (motus fúero, movébor)Ps 9 Ps 14 Ps 29 Ps 61ser abalado (se eu for abalado)openPs 12:5b; Non movébor 9:27 (Ps 9 agent: Não serei abalado, agreeing), 29:7, 61:3; 93:18 Motus est pes meus. Heard as shaken in spirit first, defeated second — the Latin's range. vacilar, cair are options Ps 14:5b non movébitur in ætérnum → para sempre não será abalado: D23's words, the adverb before the negation as 118:93, so that 'never' is the only hearing (the blind reader: 'Permanecerá firme'). The stylist's worst line ('soa estrangeira'); he wants jamais será abalado (the Diurnal's), which drops in ætérnum's word — option in Ps 14. 124:1 non commovébitur in ætérnum and 111:6 in ætérnum non commovébitur will meet the same choice; commovéri (15:8 ne commóvear, 13 lines) shares the verb, one Greek (σαλεύω). commovéri, Ps 15:8 ne commóvear → para eu não ser abalado (the 118:80 build; one Greek, σαλεύω); = Acts 2:25 (fetched). Passed the Latinist twice. Merged from a duplicate row (Non movébor): Ps 9:27, 29:7, 61:3 (grep) — the proud man's boast and the just man's trust in one phrase. Ps 16:5 ut non moveántur vestígia mea → para que não sejam abaladas as minhas pegadas — the row's verb with a thing (footprints) as subject, as 93:18 Motus est pes meus will need; the blind reader heard 'that the steps stay firm' first; no other remark. não vacilem (MS1932) is the option. Ps 20:8 non commovébitur → não será abalado. The active, Ps 28:7: vox Dómini concutiéntis desértum: et commovébit Dóminus desértum Cades → a voz do Senhor que abala o deserto: e o Senhor abalará o deserto de Cades — concútere and commovére are one Greek verb (συσσείοντος … συσσείσει), so one Portuguese verb, the active of this row's ser abalado. Passed the Latinist twice. Ps 35:12 the active non móveat me → não me abale (σαλεύσαι); the blind reader heard faith / composure shaken first — the row's hearing. Passed the Latinist twice. Ps 47:6 commóti sunt → foram abalados (σαλεύω); the stylist's abalaram-se refused — colloquially 'took off'. Ps 61:3 non movébor ámplius → já não serei abalado (no remark); kept apart from 61:7 non emigrábo (não partirei). Ps 72:2 pæne moti sunt pedes → quase foram abalados — the passive kept; no reader remarked. vacilaram (MS1932) option. Ps 81:5 movebúntur ómnia fundaménta terræ → serão abalados todos os fundamentos da terra; the Latinist praised the future passive kept; the ambiguity reader heard a future earthquake. Ps 93:18 Motus est pes meus → O meu pé foi abalado (the stylist's worst line; vacilou kept as an option). Ps 95:9, 95:11 jussive Commoveátur → Abale-se (pronominal: verb first as the Latin, no gendered participle); 95:10 qui non commovébitur → que não será abalado; the verb three times in three verses, as the Latin. The ambiguity reader heard 'tremble, be shaken' and, of the sea, 'be stirred'. Seja abalada / abalado option. Ps 97:6 moveátur mare, et plenitúdo ejus → abale-se o mar, e a sua plenitude — identical with 95:11 commoveátur (σαλευθήτω both). The ambiguity reader heard abale-se as possibly 'be troubled / damaged', against the joyful context — a cost for 95:9, 95:11 and 97:6 together; seja abalado, agite-se options. Ps 98:1 moveátur terra → abale-se a terra (95:9's jussive); no reader remarked. Ps 106:27 moti sunt sicut ébrius → vacilaram como um ébrio — the row's option taken beside the drunkard; ébrio not bêbado (a proparoxytone at the mediant). Ps 111:7b non commovébitur donec → não será abalado até que (the Latin's commovébitur where the Greek has οὐ μὴ φοβηθῇ — the Latin followed).
præválere (advérsus)prevalecer (contra) (Prevaleci contra ele)openPs 12:4b(5a); 51:9 et præváluit in vanitáte sua, 64:4 Verba iniquórum prævaluérunt super nos (grep, 3 lines); the Latin's own descendant Ps 51:9 et præváluit in vanitáte sua → e prevaleceu na sua vaidade: the stylist asked se fez forte (the Greek's ἐδυναμώθη) — refused, rule 1; the blind reader heard 'won out through his pride'.
per diemPs 12 Ps 21 Ps 60 Ps 75 Ps 94 Ps 120durante o diaopenPs 12:2; heard as "all day long" first; cada dia (MS1932), o dia todo are options; tota die (37:7 …) is another phrase and should keep o dia todo Ps 21:3 clamábo per diem … et nocte → clamarei durante o dia … e de noite (MS1932's pair): the row held beside nocte; de dia is the option.
bona tríbuerePs 27 Ps 36dar coisas boas (que me deu coisas boas)openPs 12:6b; draft 1 que me concedeu bens was heard by the blind reader as property and called administrative by the stylist, whose wording this is; the Greek has τῷ εὐεργετήσαντί με. tríbuere and dare never meet in a verse, so dar is free; 15:7 qui tríbuit mihi intelléctum can read que me deu entendimento Ps 15:7 qui tríbuit mihi intelléctum → que me deu entendimento, as this row proposed; passed the Latinist twice. Ps 83:13 Non privábit bonis → Não privará de coisas boas — this row's coisas boas; the ambiguity reader heard 'good things in general'.
in finemPs 9 Ps 12 Ps 15 Ps 17 Ps 37 Ps 38 Ps 45 Ps 48 Ps 51 Ps 73 Ps 76 Ps 88 Ps 118para sempre where it says perpetuity (each psalm decides)working (D27)Ps 9:7a, 9:19 ×2, 9:32 (ne vídeat in finem → para nunca mais ver). εἰς τέλος. Draft 1 had até o fim: in the negation of 9:19 (non in finem … non períbit in finem) the Latinist (major) and the blind reader both heard a bounded 'not until the end' — i.e. it will perish at the end. para sempre everywhere since; 9:32 nunca mais where the negative is a final clause. Affects 12:1, 43:23, 67:17b, 73:1, 3, 10, 11, 19, 76:9, 78:5, 88:47, 51:7 (grep, 19 lines); not usque in finem (15:11, 37:7), and 17:36b, 48:9 want their own reading. D27: NOT merged with in ætérnum — mostly another Greek phrase (εἰς τέλος), and 48:9 has both side by side. The wordings of Pss 9 and 12 stand. Ps 17:36b, the place D27 named: corréxit me in finem → me corrigiu até o fim — not para sempre: nothing is negated (the failure at 9:19 was não … até o fim), and with a past act para sempre would make the correcting perpetual; εἰς τέλος, DRB unto the end, MS1932 até ao fim. The blind reader heard 'corrected me completely' first — the other sense of εἰς τέλος — and 'until the end of my life' second. Passed the Latinist twice. So in finem has two renderings, as D27 allowed: para sempre (perpetuity) and até o fim (Ps 17 decision finem, para sempre the option). Merged from a duplicate row: Ps 12:1 me esquecereis para sempre? (Ps 9 proposed it for 9:7a, 9:19, 9:32; followed). 22 lines have finem (grep), the adverbial in finem in most: 43:23, 51:7, 67:17b, 73:1, 73:3, 73:10, 73:11, 73:19, 76:9, 78:5, 88:47 … — with úsquequo three times (12:1, 78:5, 88:47), where "how long … for ever?" is the Latin's own. Collides with D23 in ætérnum → para sempre where both occur near each other (48:9 has both in one colon: in ætérnum, et vivet adhuc in finem) — 48:9 must decide locally; até o fim is the option. The blind reader heard 12:1 as "forgotten me for good?" D27: NOT merged with in ætérnum — mostly another Greek phrase (εἰς τέλος), and 48:9 has both side by side. The wordings of Pss 9 and 12 stand. usque in finem, Ps 15:11 delectatiónes in déxtera tua usque in finem → deleites na vossa direita até o fim (D27 keeps usque in finem apart; affirmative, so none of 9:19's negation fault); passed the Latinist twice; the blind reader heard 'to the end of my life' first, 'of time' second. para sempre is the option. 37:7 usque in finem can follow. Ps 37:7 curvátus sum usque in finem → fiquei curvado até o fim (as 15:11, usque in finem); the blind reader heard it temporal ('until the end'); DRB 'even to the end'. Kept. Ps 48:9, the place D27 named: laborábit in ætérnum, et vivet adhuc in finem → trabalhará para sempre, e viverá ainda até o fim — the two phrases kept two; affirmative, so 9:19's fault does not arise. Passed the Latinist twice. Ps 51:7 déstruet te in finem → te destruirá para sempre — the place D27 named: a future of destruction, affirmative; DRB, MS1932 'for ever'; até o fim (heard as a limit) and por completo are options. Passed the Latinist twice. Ps 73 (five places): para sempre at 73:1, 73:10 (the Úsquequo … in finem? formula), 73:11, 73:19 (não esqueçais para sempre); 73:3 Leva manus tuas … in finem → até o fim (17:36b's sense, utterly: para sempre would make the lifted hands perpetual). No reader remarked. Ps 76:9 Aut in finem misericórdiam suam abscíndet → Ou cortará até o fim a sua misericórdia (v2): the verse after in ætérnum (76:8 para sempre); the v1 Latinist and stylist independently asked the two phrases kept apart; not negated, so D27's misreading does not arise. para sempre the option.
orbis terræPs 1 Ps 2 Ps 7 Ps 9 Ps 11 Ps 15 Ps 16 Ps 17 Ps 18 Ps 21 Ps 23 Ps 32 Ps 36 Ps 43 Ps 45 Ps 46 Ps 47 Ps 48 Ps 49 Ps 51 Ps 56 Ps 57 Ps 62 Ps 64 Ps 65 Ps 66 Ps 70 Ps 71 Ps 72 Ps 73 Ps 74 Ps 75 Ps 76 Ps 80 Ps 82 Ps 84 Ps 88 Ps 92 Ps 95 Ps 96 Ps 97 Ps 100 Ps 101 Ps 103 Ps 105 Ps 106 Ps 107 Ps 108 Ps 112 Ps 118 Ps 133o mundo (julgará o mundo com equidade); o orbe da terra the optionsettled (D30)Ps 9:8b (twin 95:13, grep). The Latin's word; the blind reader listed orbe as unknown; options o mundo, a terra inteira. Ps 17:16a fundaménta orbis terrárum → os fundamentos do mundo: orbe failed again — unknown to the blind reader (as in Ps 9) and 'livresca' for the stylist. The Latin psalter never has mundus for the world (grep: mundus is only 'clean', 18:13, 23:4, 50:4, 50:9, 50:12), so mundo collides with nothing. Proposed: the row → o mundo in all 12 lines (9:8b, 18:5, 23:1, 49:12, 71:8, 88:12, 92:1b, 95:10, 95:13, 97:6, 97:9 — o orbe da terra the option); Ps 9:8b would follow. Ps 18:5 in fines orbis terræ → até os confins do mundo — D30 held at the verse St Paul quotes (Rom 10:18, word for word in the Vulgate; τῆς οἰκουμένης). Ps 23:1 applied: o mundo, e todos os que nele habitam — the masculine lets nele (in eo) and 23:2 o fundou … o preparou (eum) point to the world, as the Latin's pronouns point to orbis (the Hebrew's are feminine, the earth). Passed the Latinist twice; no reader stopped. Ps 32:8 omnes inhabitántes orbem → todos os que habitam o mundo (D30). Ps 49:12 meus est enim orbis terræ → pois meu é o mundo (D30); the Latinist's o orbe da terra refused. Ps 76:19 orbi terræ → o mundo — applied; coruscatiónes → relâmpagos (ἀστραπαί, as 17:15 fúlgura), so the near-twin 96:4 Illuxérunt fúlgura ejus orbi terræ can copy iluminaram o mundo. Ps 92:1b firmávit orbem terræ, qui non commovébitur → Pois ele firmou o mundo, que não será abalado (D30); the participle agrees with o mundo because the relative names the subject (D43's não se abalará is for the subjectless verb). 95:10 is the near-twin (corréxit). Ps 89:2 terra et orbis → a terra e o mundo — applied as D30 names it; no reader remarked. Ps 95:10 Étenim corréxit orbem terræ, qui non commovébitur → Pois ele endireitou o mundo, que não será abalado (92:1b's build with the Latin's other verb); 95:13 Judicábit orbem terræ in æquitáte → Julgará o mundo com equidade (= 9:8b). Ps 96:4 Illuxérunt fúlgura ejus orbi terræ → Os seus relâmpagos iluminaram o mundo — 76:19a copied (fúlgura / coruscatiónes one Greek word, ἀστραπαί → relâmpagos, D15).

Ps 30:25 et confortétur cor vestrum → e que o vosso coração se fortaleça (26:14 in the plural).

in opportunitátibusPs 9nas horas oportunasopenPs 9:10 = 9:22 (in opportunitátibus, in tribulatióne); one slot.
despícere (God)desdenhar (desdenhais nas horas oportunas?)openPs 9:22; kept apart from despícere (enemies) → olhar de cima; the blind reader listed desdenhais as unknown but heard 'despises' right. Ps 26:9b neque despícias me → nem me desdenheis — applied. superbírePs 9 Ps 16 Ps 30 Ps 35 Ps 72 Ps 73 Ps 93 Ps 100 Ps 118encher-se de soberba (Enquanto o ímpio se enche de soberba)openPs 9:23 (the stylist, taken); MS1932's ensoberbecer-se was unknown to the blind reader.
incéndiPs 9 Ps 65 Ps 73 Ps 79ser abrasado (o pobre é abrasado)openPs 9:23; the Latin's fire kept; abrasado unknown to the blind reader, who still heard 'burnt, or suffering as if burnt'; options arde, é queimado.
exacerbárePs 9 Ps 104 Ps 105 Ps 106provocar where alone; a second word where it stands beside irritáresettled (D27)Ps 9:25 (8 verses: 9:25, 77:40, 41, 56, 104:28, 105:32, 43, 106:11). One Greek verb with irritáre (παροξύνω) — D15 merges; exasperou was unknown to the blind reader. D27: provocar settled where alone, as irritáre (one Greek verb); a verse with both decides locally. Ps 104:28 et non exacerbávit sermónes suos → e não exacerbou as suas palavras — a local exception, since the object is words, not God, and não provocou as suas palavras gives no sense. The cognate covers both 'make harsher' and 'exasperate'. The Latinist passed it on both drafts as keeping the Septuagint's oddity. The stylist called it a false friend (amargou), and the ambiguity reader listed it as unknown; refused, held for the Latin's word (decision exacerbavit, with provocou and tornou amargas as options). Ps 105:32 exacerbavérunt spíritum ejus should weigh this. Ps 105:32 (beside irritáre) quia exacerbavérunt spíritum ejus → porque amarguraram o seu espírito — D27's local decision: the root acerbus and the Greek παρεπίκραναν; o seu espírito left open between Moses' and God's. 105:43 alone → o provocaram. Passed the Latinist twice. Ps 106:11 exacerbavérunt elóquia Dei … irritavérunt → exasperaram as palavras de Deus … provocaram — D27 applied: two Greek verbs (παρεπίκραναν / παρώξυναν), so irritáre keeps provocar and exacerbáre takes exasperar (L&S, DRB). One blind reader did not know it. amarguraram option (Ps 105:32 chose it — the two psalms differ; for Gustavo).
insídiæ / insidiáriPs 9emboscada / armar emboscada (Senta-se de emboscada … arma emboscada … Arma emboscada)openPs 9:29, 30a, 30b (the only three verses, grep). One family kept; the stylist gave armar. Options MS1932 ciladas, DM1962 espreita.
labor (noun)Ps 6 Ps 9 Ps 48 Ps 72 Ps 77 Ps 87 Ps 93fadiga (fadiga e dor)openPs 9:28, 9:35a (labor et dolor twice). Kept apart from laboráre → cansar-se. Ps 24:18 a minha fadiga. Ps 72:5 In labóre hóminum → na fadiga dos homens; 72:16 labor est ante me → é fadiga diante de mim — one noun twice; the stylist asked the bare é fadiga (v2) to echo 72:5. Ps 77:46 labóres eórum → os seus trabalhos; 77:51 primítias omnis labóris eórum → as primícias de todo o seu trabalho (v2) — the product of toil; fadigas was heard as tiredness given to the locust. A local departure; fadiga the option. Ps 89:10 labor et dolor → fadiga e dor — as 9:28.
órphanus / pupíllusPs 9 Ps 16 Ps 81 Ps 108órfãoopenpupíllus 9:39, 81:3, 93:6, 108:12, 145:9; órphanus 9:35b, 67:5b, 108:9 (grep; 16:8a pupíllam óculi is the eye's pupil, another word). Two Latin words, one Greek (ὀρφανός), one Portuguese. Ps 81:3 pupíllo → órfão, beside egéno → necessitado; no remark. Ps 93:6 e mataram os órfãos (plural, pupíllos).
requírere (God, of blood / sin)Ps 3 Ps 4 Ps 6 Ps 7 Ps 9 Ps 13 Ps 14 Ps 24 Ps 30 Ps 31 Ps 34 Ps 58 Ps 60 Ps 67 Ps 72 Ps 78 Ps 79 Ps 88 Ps 118pedir contas (ao pedir contas do sangue deles; Não pedirá contas)openPs 9:13, 9:34 — the question of 9:13 answered in the same words by the wicked in 9:34. insípiens / insipiéntiaPs 13 Ps 21 Ps 37 Ps 38 Ps 48 Ps 68 Ps 73 Ps 91 Ps 93insensato / insensatezopenPs 13:1a (= 52:1) Disse o insensato no seu coração: * Não há Deus — ἄφρων; MS1932 in Ps 13 and DM1962. 14 lines (grep): the adjective 48:11 and 91:7 stand beside stultus, so it must stay apart from tolo / estulto; 73:18 pópulus insípiens, 75:5 insipiéntes corde, 93:8 Intellégite, insipiéntes; the noun 21:3, 37:6, 38:9, 68:6. Passed the Latinist twice; no reader remarked. Options néscio (MS1932 in Ps 52), tolo Ps 21:3, the noun (named here): et non ad insipiéntiam mihi → e não será para a minha insensatez — draft 1's verbless e não para a minha insensatez was heard by the blind reader as 'não para' = does not STOP (parar); the copula será (the stylist's) mends it. Open as the Latin (not folly in me / not to my folly). Ps 37:6 a fácie insipiéntiæ meæ → diante da minha insensatez (the noun, as the row names); the blind reader listed insensatez unknown; kept. Ps 48:11 insípiens … stultus → o insensato e o tolo (stultus → tolo, new row); 48:13 = 48:21 juméntis insipiéntibus → aos animais insensatos — the adjective kept on the beasts so that the refrain echoes 48:11 (MS1932 sem razão option). Ps 52:1 copies 13:1a; the blind reader of Ps 52 listed insensato as unknown (the first time) — kept. Ps 75:5 omnes insipiéntes corde → todos os insensatos de coração; the ambiguity reader listed insensatos unknown, kept. Ps 91:7 Vir insípiens → O homem insensato — applied beside tolo. Ps 93:8 insipiéntes in pópulo → insensatos entre o povo, with stulti → tolos (D43).
prospícereolhar (O Senhor olhou do céu para os filhos dos homens)openPs 13:2 (= 52:3 with Deus). L&S 'to look forward, into the distance, look out'; διέκυψεν. Draft 1 had olhou do céu sobre for super; the stylist heard a calque and the preposition yields (D2). Other places 36:13 próspicit (foresees), 84:12 justítia de cælo prospéxit, 101:20 prospéxit de excélso (grep) — the pro- is not heard; must stay apart from respícere (estar voltado para, olhai) and aspícere (Olhai para mim). Option se debruçou do céu sobre (the Greek's image) Ps 36:13 quóniam próspicit quod véniet dies ejus → porque prevê que virá o seu dia (προβλέπει, the row's 'sees ahead' sense); passed the Latinist twice, heard rightly (the Lord foresees). Ps 84:12 justítia de cælo prospéxit → e a justiça olhou do céu, as named; the ambiguity reader heard 'looked down from heaven'. Ps 101:20 prospéxit de excélso sancto suo … aspéxit → olhou da sua santa altura … olhou do céu para a terra — the row's bare olhou against olhou para (aspícere, and 101:18 respéxit in, one Greek verb): DRB's 'looked forth … looked upon' made by the preposition. se debruçou option.
contrítioPs 13 Ps 59ruína (Ruína e infelicidade nos seus caminhos)openPs 13:3d (= Rom 3:16; σύντριμμα); only singular here — 59:4, 146:3 contritiónes (breaches, wounds) will want another word. The noun of contérere → quebrar, but quebranto is the evil eye in Brazil. Cost: ruína is also a Latin word of the psalter (105:29, 109:6, 143:14). Passed the Latinist twice; the blind reader heard 'they cause ruin' first. Options destruição (DRB; proposed for intéritus), aflição (MS1932) Ps 59:4 sana contritiónes ejus → curai as suas fraturas (συντρίμματα, the breakings of the earth, healed); as the row foresaw, ruína cannot be healed. brechas (DRB), chagas (MS1932) options. 146:3 álligat contritiónes eórum should weigh fraturas. No reader objected.
infelícitasPs 13infelicidadeworkingPs 13:3d only (grep); ταλαιπωρία; the cognate, current
simulPs 13 Ps 27 Ps 34 Ps 36 Ps 39 Ps 48 Ps 54 Ps 68 Ps 73 Ps 87 Ps 96 Ps 97 Ps 113juntosopenPs 13:3a (= 52:4) juntos se tornaram inúteis (DRB together); 15 lines (grep): 30:14, 87:18 together; 48:11 simul insípiens, et stultus is 'alike'; 48:3 simul in unum meets the row in unum → juntos and must decide locally. Options juntamente (MS1932 in Ps 52), ao mesmo tempo Ps 27:3 Ne simul trahas me cum peccatóribus → Não me arrasteis juntamente com os pecadores — simul … cum said of one person: juntos would need a plural; juntamente com (MS1932's) is the Portuguese for the adverb with cum. Proposal: juntamente wherever simul goes with cum and a singular. Ps 36:38 Injústi autem disperíbunt simul → Mas os injustos juntos perecerão de todo (the stylist's order, juntos next to the verb). Ps 48:3 see in unum. Ps 48:11 simul insípiens, et stultus períbunt → juntos perecerão o insensato e o tolo (36:38's order). Ps 73:8 cognátio eórum simul → os da parentela deles, juntos — = 73:6 in idípsum (one Greek). Ps 87:18 circumdedérunt me simul → cercaram-me ao mesmo tempo — the row's option, the stylist's (draft 1 cercaram-me juntos was clipped at the final, and its masculine gave the unnamed subject a gender). The v2 Latinist (minor) found it narrower than 'together' and asked todos juntos; held, option. Ps 97:8 simul montes exsultábunt → os montes exultarão juntos — the stylist's order (at the clause head juntos dangled between rivers and mountains); passed the Latinist.
esca / cibus (sicut escam panis, ut cibum panis)Ps 13 Ps 43 Ps 68 Ps 73como quem come pãoopenPs 13:4; 52:5 has ut cibum panis — one Greek (βρώσει ἄρτου) for both, so one Portuguese. The Latinist (Ps 13 draft 2, minor, having passed it on draft 1) read esca as the food and asked como alimento de pão — refused, option there. Elsewhere esca is food given (68:22, 103:21, 135:25 Qui dat escam omni carni, 144:15 …, 17 lines) and will be alimento or comida Ps 52:5 ut cibum panis → como quem come pão, copied from 13:4. The Latinist of Ps 52 asked como alimento de pão on both reads (minor), the stylist offered como se come o pão (the como … come jingle, which he said to keep) — both refused for the twin, options in Ps 52's decision cibum. The same Latinist remark has now been refused three times across the twins.
trepidárePs 13 Ps 26tremerworkingPs 13:5 = 52:6b only (grep) Ps 26:1b a quo trepidábo? → diante de quem tremerei? — the stylist: tremer de alguém is not Portuguese; MS1932's preposition taken. The pair a quem temerei? / diante de quem tremerei? keeps the Latin's two verbs.
captívitasPs 13 Ps 52 Ps 67 Ps 84cativeiroworkingPs 13:7 (= 52:7), 67:19a cepísti captivitátem, 77:61, 84:2, 125:1, 125:4 (grep). With avértere → afastar o cativeiro (13:7, 84:2); with convértere (52:7, 125:1, 125:4) the row convértere decides Ps 52:7 cum convérterit Deus captivitátem plebis suæ → quando Deus fizer voltar o cativeiro do seu povo — the convértere row's verb, causative, as the stylist asked. Draft 1 had reverter o cativeiro (the same root; 'undo'), refused by the stylist as juridical and listed unknown by the blind reader; the feared hearing 'bring the captivity back again' was raised by no reader (not yet tested blind in this form). 125:1 In converténdo … captivitátem Sion, 125:4 Convérte, Dómine, captivitátem nostram (→ Fazei voltar, Senhor, o nosso cativeiro) should follow. fizer voltar os cativos, reverter options. Ps 67:19a cepísti captivitátem → levastes cativo o cativeiro (Eph 4:8's form). The gate called it imported and asked tomastes o cativeiro; held — the Pauline reading is the verse's tradition, tomastes o cativeiro is opaque aloud; option. Ps 84:2 avertísti captivitátem Jacob → afastastes o cativeiro de Jacó, as named; no reader remarked (the ambiguity reader: the people's captivity).
Quis dabit …?Ps 13 Ps 24 Ps 28 Ps 48 Ps 54 Ps 84Quem dará …?openPs 13:7 = 52:7 Quis dabit ex Sion salutáre Israël? → Quem dará de Sião a salvação de Israel? — the question kept, which in Latin is also a wish; 54:7 Quis dabit mihi pennas sicut colúmbæ is the other place (grep). ingrédi (walking)Ps 14 Ps 25 Ps 40 Ps 67 Ps 117andar (Aquele que anda sem mancha)openPs 14:2 Qui ingréditur sine mácula — L&S 'to go into, enter' and 'to go, walk'; the Greek πορευόμενος fixes 'walk', the verb the glossary renders andar for ambuláre and abíre (1:1). 25:1, 25:11 ego in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum (grep) can follow (andei na minha inocência). entrar stays for íngredi into a place (117:19 the gates). Passed the Latinist twice and the blind reader. Options caminha (DM1962), entra Ps 25:1, 25:11 in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum → andei na minha inocência — applied; the blind reader heard the conduct rightly.
sine máculaPs 14sem manchaworkingPs 14:2 only (grep); immaculátus keeps imaculado (118:1, 118:80)
décipereenganar (e não engana)openPs 14:4b (Greek ἀθετῶν); 61:10 ut decípiant, 76:3 non sum decéptus (grep: 3 lines). Takes the verb enganar, so dolus in the same psalm keeps the noun engano (14:3a não usou de engano). No object supplied (MS1932 não o engana is the option) Ps 61:10 → enganem (finite, v2). Ps 76:3 non sum decéptus → e não fui enganado — applied; no reader remarked.
usúraPs 14usura (que não deu o seu dinheiro à usura)openPs 14:4b; 54:12 usúra, et dolus, 71:14 Ex usúris et iniquitáte (grep). The cognate keeps the reproach those two verses need; listed as unknown by the blind reader. múneraPs 14 Ps 25 Ps 44 Ps 71 Ps 75dádivasopenPs 14:4b nem aceitou dádivas contra o inocente (heard as a bribe without the word); must serve the kings' gifts 67:30, 71:10, 75:12 (grep), so not subornos (DRB). Option presentes Ps 25:10 déxtera eórum repléta est munéribus → a direita deles está cheia de dádivas — the stylist asked for presentes (dádivas 'solemn'); refused for this row, presentes kept as the option; the blind reader heard gifts first, bribes by inference, as at 14:4b. Ps 44:13 filhas de Tiro com dádivas — held (the mediant proparoxytone, as munéribus); the stylist asked ofertas, refused (D41's oferta). Ps 67:30 tibi ófferent reges múnera → os reis vos oferecerão dádivas; the ambiguity reader listed dádivas unknown; kept. Ps 71:10 múnera ófferent … dona addúcent → oferecerão dádivas … levarão presentes — dádivas for múnera, presentes for dona (two Latin words, two Portuguese). The stylist asked dons (proparoxytone at the mediant) — held as at 44:13, option; the ambiguity reader listed dádivas unknown. Ps 75:12 affértis múnera → trazeis dádivas — the row at the final, a proparoxytone as múnera is; the stylist asked ofertas (refused: oblátio's family, D41; presentes the option); the ambiguity reader listed dádivas unknown.
dedúcere / redígere ad níhilumPs 30 Ps 54 Ps 59 Ps 107reduzir a nada (o malvado foi reduzido a nada)openPs 14:4a (ἐξουδένωται). The same phrase 58:9, 59:14 = 107:14 (ad níhilum dedúcet → reduzirá a nada), with redígere 72:20, 77:59, 72:21 ad níhilum redáctus sum (grep; the Greek of those not checked). reduzir is re-dúcere. Heard by the blind reader as 'destroyed before him' first, 'esteemed worthless' second — both in the Latin Ps 59:14 ad níhilum dedúcet → reduzirá a nada — applied; heard as 'destroy' first. Ps 57:8 Ad níhilum devénient → Serão reduzidos a nada — devenire is intransitive, but the Greek is 14:4a's passive (ἐξουδενωθήσονται), so the same phrase; Chegarão a nada (heard as 'fail') option. Ps 58:9 ad níhilum dedúces omnes gentes → reduzireis a nada todas as nações — applied; no remark. Ps 72:20 ad níhilum rédiges → reduzireis a nada; 72:21 ad níhilum redáctus sum → fui reduzido a nada — identical in both; dedúcere me at 72:24 → me guiastes (D22).

protéctorPs 17 Ps 27 Ps 30 Ps 32 Ps 39 Ps 83 Ps 113 Ps 120protetor (O meu protetor; o Senhor se fez o meu protetor)openPs 17:3c, 17:19, 17:31 (one decision protector, three slots); 19 lines in the psalter (grep), often beside adjútor (27:7, 32:20, 39:18, 113:17–19 adjútor eórum et protéctor eórum est) and refúgium. ὑπερασπιστής, the one who holds a shield over. The cognate, an agent noun as the Latin's; stays apart from suscéptor → amparo (D19) and adjútor → auxílio. The Latinist passed it four times; no reader remarked. Options defensor (MS1932's word for suscéptor — they would cross), escudo (DM1962, the Hebrew's image; refused). Ps 17:2–3 sets the four titles side by side — see the rows adjútor and suscéptor for the mixed series it makes Ps 26:1b Dóminus protéctor vitæ meæ → O Senhor é o protetor da minha vida — applied. Ps 83:10 Protéctor noster → nosso protetor (vocatives joined: Deus, nosso protetor).
firmaméntum (God as support)Ps 17 Ps 18 Ps 24 Ps 70 Ps 71 Ps 72 Ps 88 Ps 104esteio (o Senhor é o meu esteio)settled (D31)Ps 17:2 (also 24:14 Firmaméntum est Dóminus timéntibus eum, 70:3 Quóniam firmaméntum meum, et refúgium meum es tu). στερέωμα, 'a support, a prop' (L&S). The blind reader heard o meu firmamento FIRST as 'my sky' — Portuguese firmamento is only the vault. The Latin keeps one word for the vault (18:2, 150:1 in firmaménto virtútis ejus) and the stay; Portuguese cannot, so: firmamento where it is the sky, esteio where God holds up (24:14, 70:3); 71:16, 72:4 firmaméntum in plaga eórum, 104:16 omne firmaméntum panis decide locally (all nine lines by grep). Options in Ps 17: o meu firmamento, o meu firme apoio (MS1932), a minha firmeza. The Latinist passed esteio; the stylist did not remark Ps 24:14 applied (O Senhor é o esteio dos que o temem); the blind reader listed esteio unknown. Ps 70:3b (named in D31) → o meu esteio — the ambiguity reader listed esteio as unknown; kept. Ps 71:16 Et erit firmaméntum in terra → E haverá esteio na terra (the local decision D31 left open): draft 1 sustento was heard as food first by the Latinist (minor, 'slides to the Hebrew's grain') and the ambiguity reader; esteio (στήριγμα, a prop) taken in v2 and passed the gate. Options sustento, mantimento, firmamento. Ps 88:41 posuísti firmaméntum ejus formídinem (ὀχυρώματα, of the king) → fizestes da sua fortaleza um pavor — decided locally (D31). fortaleza holds both 'stronghold' and 'firmness'; firmeza (72:4) is an option. No Latinist remark. Ps 104:16 omne firmaméntum panis contrívit → quebrou todo o esteio do pão — the place D31 left open: στήριγμα ἄρτου, a support. MS1932 sustento is the option. The ambiguity reader listed esteio as unknown, and it is kept for D31.
liberátorPs 69libertadorworkingPs 17:2, 17:48 (meu libertador dos meus inimigos irados); 69:6, 143:2 (grep) — A crossing to note (review 2026-09-21): the noun libertador sits in erípere’s family (libertar), not in liberáre’s (livrar, the row above). A reader crossing columns sees liberáre → livrar but liberátor → libertador; livrador is not current. Left as it stands; decide in Ps 69 / 143 if the two families must be kept apart there. Ps 69:6b → o meu libertador — no liberáre or erípere in the psalm, so nothing to keep apart; no reader remarked.
præoccupárePs 17surpreender (os laços da morte me surpreenderam)openPs 17:6 only (grep); one Greek verb with 17:19 prævenérunt (προέφθασαν), which shares it. L&S 'seize upon beforehand … take, catch'. MS1932's verb Ps 94:2 Præoccupémus fáciem ejus (friendly; προφθάσωμεν) → Cheguemo-nos primeiro à sua face — the stylist's line (v2). Draft 1's Adiantemo-nos à sua face (the prævenire row's verb, one Greek) was the stylist's worst line and the ambiguity reader heard 'hurry / get ahead of him' and did not know the word. primeiro carries prae-. So the row has two senses: hostile surpreender (17:6), friendly chegar-se primeiro (94:2). Passed the v2 Latinist. The Septuagesima Invitatory antiphon (Quadp1-0) has the same words with Dómini.
calígoPs 10 Ps 15 Ps 17 Ps 22 Ps 74 Ps 96 Ps 115névoa escura (e havia uma névoa escura sob os seus pés)openPs 17:10 (γνόφος); 96:2 Nubes et calígo in circúitu ejus will meet it beside nubes → nuvem. trevas is ténebræ's (17:12); caligem needs a footnote. havia supplied at the stylist's request Ps 96:2 Nubes, et calígo in circúitu ejus → Nuvem e névoa escura estão ao seu redor — the place this row named; the same Greek (γνόφος). No reader remarked.
latíbulumPs 17esconderijo (E fez das trevas o seu esconderijo)workingPs 17:12 only (grep); ἀποκρυφή; refúgio is refúgium's
carbónes (ignis)Ps 17 Ps 119carvões (de fogo)workingPs 17:9 carvões foram acesos por ele, 17:13 = 17:14 granizo e carvões de fogo; 119:4 carbónibus desolatóriis, 139:11 cadent super eos carbónes (grep). MS1932's word; brasas (DM1962) is the option — brasas foram acesas says the fire twice
vocem dare (dedit vocem suam)Ps 5 Ps 6 Ps 17 Ps 57 Ps 76 Ps 102 Ps 118fazer ouvir a voz (e o Altíssimo fez ouvir a sua voz)openPs 17:14; 45:7 dedit vocem suam, mota est terra and 67:34b dabit voci suæ vocem virtútis will meet it (grep). The idiom, as MS1932 and DM1962; deu a sua voz is not said. Ps 76:18 vocem dedérunt nubes (no possessive) → as nuvens fizeram ouvir a voz — both Latinist runs asked deram (a sua) voz, and the stylist deram a sua voz; held for the row, options.
fumus / grandoPs 17 Ps 36 Ps 67 Ps 104fumaça / granizoworkingPs 17:9, 17:13–14; fumo is tobacco in Brazil, saraiva European; 148:8 grando, 101:4 sicut fumus Ps 101:4 sicut fumus → como a fumaça — applied.
pónere + predicate (made X Y)the verb the Portuguese build wants: fazer de (17:12 fez das trevas o seu esconderijo), tornar + adjective (17:33 tornou imaculado o meu caminho), fazer … como (17:35 fizestes os meus braços como um arco de bronze)openPs 17 (decision posuit, three slots). Draft 4 had fazer all three times; the stylist heard fez imaculado as a calque. pôr (the Latin's verb) is the option; láqueum pónere → pôr um laço stands Ps 20:10 Pones eos ut clíbanum ignis → Vós os fareis como um forno de fogo; 20:13 pones eos dorsum → fareis deles costas (the fazer de build of 17:12). Ps 38:6 mensurábiles posuísti dies meos → pusestes em medida os meus dias (MS1932; the Latin's verb kept): draft 1 tornastes mensuráveis — mensuráveis unknown to the blind reader, technical to the stylist; his fizestes medidos refused as this row's calque. Ps 82:12 Pone príncipes eórum sicut Oreb → Fazei os seus príncipes como Oreb; 82:14 pone illos ut rotam → fazei-os como uma roda — the row applied; cost: 82:10 Fac illis → Fazei-lhes shares the verb (another build). Ponde option; no reader remarked.
assúmere (me)recolher (e me recolheu de muitas águas)openPs 17:17, beside accépit me → me tomou (ἔλαβεν … προσελάβετο). The other two places (grep): 26:10 Dóminus autem assúmpsit me (o Senhor me recolheu — fits), 64:5 quem elegísti, et assumpsísti. Options tomar consigo, MS1932 tirar Ps 26:10 Dóminus autem assúmpsit me → o Senhor, porém, me recolheu — applied; the blind reader heard taking in (death a second hearing). autem → porém after the subject, where the Latin has it (the stylist). Ps 49:16 assúmis testaméntum meum per os tuum → tomas a minha aliança na tua boca — a thing, not a person, so not recolher; tomar na boca is the idiom (DRB in thy mouth, MS1932). The Latinist asked pela tua boca twice: option (not said with tomar). Ps 64:5 departs: quem elegísti, et assumpsísti → aquele que escolhestes e tomastes para vós — the Latinist's fix (προσελάβου), taken because all three readers stopped at recolhestes (sheltering; a jingle with escolhestes; gathering things up). recolher stays for a man drawn out of danger (17:17, 26:10); God taking a chosen man to himself is tomar para si.
edúcerePs 36fazer sair (E me fez sair para a amplidão)openPs 17:20 — the stylist's best line of stage one. conduzir fails rule 3 at the imperative (conduzi-me, D22). Twelve other lines (grep), most with de (30:5, 39:3, 77:16, 106:14 edúxit eos de ténebris, 106:28, 142:11b; 141:8 Educ de custódia is an imperative) — those may want tirar de Ps 29:4 eduxísti ab inférno ánimam meam → tirastes do inferno a minha alma — tirar de for the source, as this row foresees (MS1932 tiraste); fizestes sair the option. Passed the Latinist twice. Ps 30:5 Edúces me de láqueo hoc → Vós me tirareis deste laço (tirar de with a source, 29:4). Ps 36:6 Et edúcet quasi lumen justítiam tuam → E fará sair a tua justiça como a luz; the stylist asked fará surgir (breath) — refused for the row. Ps 39:3 edúxit me de lacu misériæ → me tirou da cova da miséria — the tirar de of 29:4 and 30:5 where a source is named; passed all three readers. pinguisPs 19 Ps 21 Ps 62 Ps 64 Ps 67 Ps 77gordoopenPs 19:4 holocáustum … pingue (the stylist's rico em gordura and pingue are options); the blind reader heard the fat animal first, an abundant offering second — both the Latin's. The blind reader heard 21:30 FIRST as people with fat bodies, the prosperous second — the Latin's image; os ricos (MS1932) is the option there. Ps 77:31 occídit pingues eórum → matou os mais robustos dentre eles (v2) — v1 os gordos was heard as comic, literally fat people, by the stylist and the ambiguity reader; the gate Latinist (minor) asked os gordos back — held, option. A local departure for persons; 21:30 stands. For Gustavo.

decorPs 20 Ps 25 Ps 29 Ps 44 Ps 49 Ps 92 Ps 103esplendor (poreis sobre ele glória e grande esplendor)openPs 20:6; 8 lines (25:8, 29:8, 44:12, 49:1, 92:1a decórem indútus est, 103:1, 146:1 decóra). Kept apart from pulchritúdo → beleza, because 95:6 Conféssio, et pulchritúdo and 103:1 Confessiónem, et decórem are twins that the reader should hear as two words. beleza, formosura options Ps 29:8 præstitísti decóri meo virtútem → destes vigor ao meu esplendor (τῷ κάλλει μου; DRB beauty, MS1932 prosperidade): the row's word; the blind reader heard 'strengthened my greatness or my radiance'. Passed the Latinist twice. Ps 25:8 diléxi decórem domus tuæ → amei o esplendor da vossa casa — applied; the stylist's best line (the Dedication versicle, C8.txt). Ps 44:12 Et concupíscet Rex decórem tuum → E o Rei ansiará pelo teu esplendor — held against the Latinist twice (minor: 'comeliness', formosura): formosura is spécies' two verses before (44:5a), beleza pulchritúdo's, so the psalm's three words of beauty stay three. Ps 49:1b see spécies: a beleza do seu esplendor. Ps 92:1a decórem indútus est → vestiu-se de esplendor — the row; the Latinist (minor, v1 and v2 gate) asked beleza, held as at 44:12; the stylist named 92:1a the best line. Ps 95:6 Conféssio, et pulchritúdo → Confissão e beleza — beleza for pulchritúdo as this row reserved; 103:1 Confessiónem, et decórem will be esplendor. Ps 103:1b → e de esplendor with 92:1a's verb (Vestistes-vos de), kept apart from 95:6 pulchritúdo → beleza. The Latinist asked formosura (v1; refused under this row).
gáudiumPs 20 Ps 29 Ps 50júbilo (o alegrareis de júbilo com o vosso rosto)open — for a rulingPs 20:7; 4 lines (29:12, 50:10 gáudium et lætítiam, 125:2a). alegria is lætítia's (50:10 has both); gozo is heard sexually in Brazil. But júbilo was unknown to the blind reader and collides with júbilus / jubiláre (46:6 in júbilo, and 12 lines of jubiláre). Options gozo, alegria; regozijo also free Ps 29:12 Convertísti planctum meum in gáudium mihi … et circumdedísti me lætítia → Convertestes o meu lamento em júbilo para mim … e me cercastes de alegria — the row followed; gáudium and lætítia in one verse (the Greek χορόν / εὐφροσύνην), so alegria cannot serve both. The Ps 29 blind reader did not list júbilo as unknown (the Ps 20 reader did); the Latinist passed it twice; no stylist remark. Evidence for the ruling: júbilo holds here; regozijo is the option in Ps 29. Ps 46 proposes jubiláre / jubilátio / júbilus → aclamar / aclamação (46:2 aclamai a Deus, 46:6 Subiu Deus entre aclamações), which removes the collision this row names and leaves júbilo to gáudium. Ps 50:10 applied: Ao meu ouvido dareis júbilo e alegria (also the Matins versicle); passed the Latinist twice. The verb, Ps 95:11 gaudébunt campi → os campos se regozijarão — a third verb of joy beside læténtur → alegrem-se and exsúltet → exulte in one verse (χαρήσεται against εὐφραινέσθωσαν / ἀγαλλιάσθω, D15's test); regozijar-se was free. MS1932 alegrar-se-ão option. No reader remarked.

ecclésiaPs 21 Ps 25assembleia (no meio da assembleia vos louvarei; na grande assembleia)settled (D34); was: open — for a ruling (with concílium)Ps 21:23, 21:26. Ten lines, ἐκκλησία in all that were read (grep; Greek read at 25:5, 25:12, 39:10): 21:23 (= Heb 2:12, whose Clementine has in medio ecclesiæ, fetched), 21:26, 25:5 Odívi ecclésiam malignántium, 25:12 in ecclésiis benedícam te, 34:18 and 39:10 in ecclésia magna (21:26's words), 67:27 In ecclésiis benedícite Deo, 88:6 and 149:1 in ecclésia sanctórum, 106:32 in ecclésia plebis. igreja (MS1932 no meio da Igreja, DRB church; the Church's reading of 21:23 through Heb 2:12) was weighed on D19's reasoning for Christus and refused: it cannot serve 25:5 (a igreja dos malvados), and at 67:27 and 21:26 (na grande igreja) it is heard as a building. So one word for all ten, which forces concílium elsewhere (row concílium). Passed the Latinist twice; no reader remarked; the blind reader heard irmãos (21:23) as the religious community. Option in Ps 21's decision concilium: da igreja / na grande igreja. Ps 25:5 Odívi ecclésiam malignántium → Odeio a assembleia dos malvados; 25:12 in ecclésiis benedícam te, Dómine → nas assembleias vos bendirei, Senhor (D34 applied; the Lavabo's last line). No reader remarked. Ps 34:18 in ecclésia magna → na grande assembleia (D34 applied).
éruerePs 21 Ps 24 Ps 36 Ps 38arrancar (Arrancai da espada, Deus, a minha alma)openPs 21:21. 13 lines (grep: 21:21, 24:17, 24:20, 31:7, 36:40, 38:9, 42:1, 49:15, 85:13, 88:49 ×2, 143:11 …), nearly always érue me with a source (de, a, ab); L&S 'pluck out, dig out; rescue'. The Greek is ῥύομαι, as behind liberáre and erípere, but the Latin keeps three verbs and 36:40 sets liberábit … éruet side by side, so not livrar. Shares arrancar with erípere-with-a-source (the two never stand in one verse — grep before a psalm that has both); 24:20 et érue me (no source) and 49:15 éruam te will want the erípere row's libertar. MS1932 Livra. Passed the Latinist twice; no reader remarked. Ps 24:17, 24:20 → libertai-me both times — the psalm says érue me twice (24:17 with a source, 24:20 without), so one wording is heard twice; arrancai-me fails at 24:20. arrancar then serves evéllere in 24:15. Proposal: arrancar with a source, libertar without, and libertar in both places where one psalm has both. Passed the Latinist twice. Ps 30:3 accélera ut éruas me (no source) → apressai-vos a libertar-me, the row's proposal (libertar without a source); passed the Latinist twice, no reader remark. Ps 36:40 et liberábit eos: et éruet eos a peccatóribus → e os livrará: * e os arrancará dos pecadores — the row's case (side by side with liberáre, with a source). Passed the Latinist twice; no reader remarked. Ps 38:9 Ab ómnibus iniquitátibus meis érue me → Arrancai-me de todas as minhas iniquidades (a source named, as 31:7); passed the Latinist twice. Ps 39:14 ut éruas me (no source) → libertar (que me liberteis), as 30:3. Ps 49:15 éruam te → eu te libertarei — the row's proposal (no source → libertar). Passed the Latinist twice; no reader remarked. Ps 85:13 eruísti ánimam meam ex inférno inferióri → arrancastes a minha alma do inferno mais profundo, with its source, as named.
fóderePs 21 Ps 56perfurar with a body as object (Perfuraram as minhas mãos e os meus pés); cavar with a pit (56:7, 93:13)openPs 21:17b — the Latin's (and the Greek's ὤρυξαν) reading, not the Hebrew's. L&S fodio 'to dig' and, transferred, 'to prick, pierce, wound, stab'; with hands and feet the Latin verb says piercing. traspassar (MS1932) is confígere's (118:120; another Greek verb); cavaram (DRB dug) is the option. The Gospels do not quote this colon (Mt 27, Mk 15, Jn 19 read in the Vulgate, fetched). Passed the Latinist twice; heard as done by the wicked.
elongárePs 21 Ps 54 Ps 72 Ps 87pôr / ficar longe (não ponhais longe de mim o vosso auxílio)openPs 21:20 (μακρύνῃς). 6 lines (grep: 21:20, 54:8 elongávi fúgiens, 70:12 Deus, ne elongéris a me, 72:27 qui elóngant se a te, 87:19 Elongásti a me amícum, 108:18). The stylist called pôr longe a calque and asked afastar; refused (the Latin says longe). Ps 54:8 Ecce, elongávi fúgiens → Eis que fui para longe, fugindo (intransitive); the stylist asked me afastei (discédere's) — refused, option. Ps 70:12 ne elongéris a me → não fiqueis longe de mim — as this row proposed; no remark. Ps 72:27 qui elóngant se a te → os que se põem longe de vós — applied; the stylist called it a laboured calque and asked se afastam (discédere's verb), kept as option — for Gustavo, with 21:20. Ps 87:19 Elongásti a me amícum et próximum → Pusestes longe de mim o amigo e o próximo, and 87:9 Longe fecísti notos meos a me → Pusestes longe de mim os meus conhecidos — one Greek verb (ἐμάκρυνας) in both, one Portuguese phrase (D15; 39:12). No reader asked for afastar this time; Afastastes (MS1932) is the option.

testaPs 21 Ps 24 Ps 49 Ps 54 Ps 88 Ps 102 Ps 110caco (secou-se como um caco)openPs 21:16 only (grep); a potsherd. MS1932 barro cozido; caco de barro the option. No reader remarked
venter / úbera / úterusPs 1 Ps 16 Ps 21 Ps 43 Ps 57 Ps 70 Ps 77 Ps 82 Ps 109 Ps 118ventre / os peitos / o seio maternoopenPs 21:10–11, 21:15b. Three body-words in two verses: venter (γαστήρ, κοιλία) → ventre in all three places (21:10, 21:11, 21:15b); ab ubéribus matris meæ → desde os peitos da minha mãe (the Latinist asked for the plural — MS1932's word; os seios would be heard as the same thing as the womb after it); ex útero → desde o seio materno: bare seio is today the breast, útero is clinical, and ventre is venter's — materno stands for no Latin word, it is what makes seio mean womb. úterus elsewhere (grep): 57:4, 70:6 In te confirmátus sum ex útero: de ventre matris meæ tu es protéctor meus (a near twin of 21:10–11 — should follow), 109:3 ex útero ante lucíferum génui te (decides for itself), 138:13 de útero matris meæ (there do ventre da minha mãe may collide with nothing — decide locally). Heard: no meio do meu ventre as 'inside the belly'; seio materno as birth. Ps 57:4 a vulva … ab útero → Desde o ventre … desde o seio materno (μήτρας … γαστρός): úterus as this row; vulva (once in the psalter) takes ventre, venter's word, since venter is not in the psalm. The stylist asked for bare seio to shorten the colon; refused (the breast). Ps 70:6 ex útero … de ventre matris meæ → desde o seio materno … desde o ventre da minha mãe — as this row proposed (21:10–11's pair); no reader remarked. Ps 109:3 ex útero … génui te (God speaking) → do ventre: materno would say what the Latin does not, and bare seio is the breast. venter is not in the psalm (as at 57:4). do seio and MS1932's das minhas entranhas are the options. The ambiguity reader heard God speaking, and asked whose the womb was, as the Latin leaves it.
