propitiári (+ dative)Ps 24 Ps 64 Ps 102ser propício (sereis propício ao meu pecado)openPs 24:11 (ἱλάσῃ). Tested: the blind reader heard 'forgive the sin' first, 'favour the sin' second, and listed propício unknown. Kept because perdoar is dimíttere's two verses later (24:18); wants a ruling for the family (64:4, 77:38, 78:9 propítius esto peccátis nostris, 98:8, 102:3 Qui propitiátur, 129:4a propitiátio — grep). Options perdoareis, sereis indulgente Ps 64:4 impietátibus nostris tu propitiáberis → vós sereis propício às nossas impiedades — applied as 24:11; the Latinist passed it twice, but the blind reader heard God favouring our sins and listed propício as unknown — the second reader to do so. Wants a ruling before 77:38, 78:9; perdoareis the option. Ps 78:9 et propítius esto peccátis nostris → e sede clemente com os nossos pecados (decision propitius) — rendered so that it cannot be heard as favouring sin, as asked after 64:4. Clemência is mercy shown to a fault: one is clement only with what is a wrong, and it asks what the Latin asks (mildness in judging; DRB 'forgive', MS1932 'perdoa'). clemens / cleméntia never occur in the Latin psalter (grep), so it collides with nothing; perdoar stays dimíttere's (24:18; the Our Father), misericordioso miséricors's (77:38 has both words). Tested: the ambiguity reader heard 'forgive our sins' first and 'be lenient toward them' second — no reading of favouring; the Latinist passed it on both drafts; the stylist did not remark. The verse is said alone (Lenten Tract 78:8–9; this psalm's Thursday Matins antiphon Ádjuva nos … et propítius esto peccátis nostris; the Nat2-0 versicle), which is why it was ruled here and not left to the row. Proposed for the family where the object is a sin: 24:11 sereis clemente com o meu pecado, 64:4 vós sereis clemente com as nossas impiedades, 77:38, 102:3 que é clemente com todas as tuas iniquidades; propício stays where the object is a person or land (98:8 propítius fuísti eis, the canticle's 32:65 propítius erit terræ); 129:4a propitiátio decides locally. Cost: the Latin's word is not kept where its object is a sin. Options in Ps 78: sede propício aos, perdoai, sede-nos propício apesar dos, sede indulgente com. Ps 77:38 et propítius fiet peccátis eórum → e será clemente com os pecados deles (decision propitius) — Ps 78's proposal taken for the family where the object is a sin, as this row asked after 64:4. Tested: the ambiguity reader heard 'will forgive their sins' first, 'be lenient toward them' second — no reading of favouring sin; the Latinist passed it on both drafts; the stylist did not remark. misericordioso (miséricors) stands in the same line and stays apart. Options será propício aos (24:11 / 64:4's build), perdoará (dimíttere's). 24:11, 64:4 and 102:3 still await Gustavo's ruling on the family. Ps 98:8 propítius fuísti eis → vós lhes fostes propício — the row's person-object case, as named; the ambiguity reader listed propício unknown (the third reader to do so); no misreading of favouring arose. clemente option. Ps 102:3 Qui propitiátur ómnibus iniquitátibus tuis → Que é clemente com todas as tuas iniquidades — the row's proposal applied word for word (decision propitiatur; é propício a, perdoa options). The ambiguity reader heard 'merciful toward your iniquities' and listed clemente as unknown; the Latinist passed it on both drafts. Still awaits Gustavo's ruling on the family (24:11, 64:4, 102:3).
demoráriPs 24 Ps 29demorar-se (A sua alma se demorará entre coisas boas)openPs 24:13, 29:6 Ad vésperum demorábitur fletus (grep); in bonis → entre coisas boas (not property); heard as abiding long among good things Ps 29:6b Ad vésperum demorábitur fletus → À tarde se demorará o pranto: * e pela manhã, a alegria — the row's second place; the blind reader heard 'weeping will stay through the evening' first (right), 'will be slow to come' second. The stylist wanted the subject first (O pranto se demorará à tarde): refused, the two adverbs heading the cola are the Latin's antithesis; option in Ps 29.
evéllerePs 24 Ps 51arrancar (porque ele arrancará do laço os meus pés)openPs 24:15 (ἐκσπάσει); 51:7, 128:6 (grep). Shares arrancar with erípere / éruere with a source — none of them in the same verse; in Ps 24 éruere takes libertar Ps 51:7 evéllet te → te arrancará; passed every reader.
necéssitas (plural)Ps 24 Ps 30 Ps 106necessidades (libertai-me das minhas necessidades)openPs 24:17 (ἀνάγκαι, straits); 30:8 and the refrain 106:6, 13, 19, 28 de necessitátibus eórum (grep). Tested: heard as privations, 'especially material' — near the straits; options angústias, aflições (MS1932) Ps 30:8 salvásti de necessitátibus ánimam meam → salvastes a minha alma das necessidades; the blind reader heard privations, 'difficulties and want' — near the straits again. Ps 106:6, 13, 19, 28 → das suas necessidades — the row applied at its named places (the straits here are hunger, prison, sickness, storm); the blind reader heard 'needs / hardships'; angústias option.
dimíttere (sins)Ps 24perdoar (e perdoai todas as minhas faltas)openPs 24:18 (ἄφες); the Our Father's verb; the row dimíttere (let go) → deixar ir stands for the Nunc dimittis Ps 31:1, 31:5b remíttere → perdoar (cujas iniquidades foram perdoadas … e vós perdoastes a impiedade do meu pecado): ἀφίημι both times (consult/parallels/ps031.md), the Greek of 24:18 dimítte — one Greek verb, one Portuguese (D15's test). Also 38:14, 84:3 (grep). Passed by the Latinist twice. Ps 38:14 Remítte mihi (no object; Greek ἄνες μοι, 'let up') → Perdoai-me (DRB 'O forgive me'; remíttere → perdoar as 31:1). The gate (minor) proposed Relevai-me (pardon and relieve at once) — held as option 2: relevar alguém is uncommon; the blind reader heard 'relent' second already. Ps 84:3 Remisísti iniquitátem → Perdoastes a iniquidade, as named.
levárePs 24levantar (A vós, Senhor, levantei a minha alma)openPs 24:1 (ἦρα); 118:48 levávi manus meas; kept apart from eleváre → elevar(-se) and attóllere → erguer (23:7). The formula row Ad te … levávi ánimam meam
afférre (to God)Ps 28 Ps 75trazer (Trazei ao Senhor glória e honra)openPs 28:1–2 (four times; the thing brought is first the young rams, then glory and honour — one verb carries both) and 95:7 (the same formula, three times), 75:12 affértis múnera (grep). ἐνέγκατε. oferecer is offérre's (65:15 ófferam); render fits glory, not rams; tributar is the Hebrew-family idiom. Safe at the vós imperative (past trouxe). DRB Bring; MS1932 Oferecei / Rendei. Passed the Latinist twice; no reader remarked. Ps 44:15b–16 afferéntur → serão trazidas (not to God), beside addúcere → levar. Ps 75:12 qui in circúitu ejus affértis múnera → que ao seu redor trazeis dádivas; no reader remarked on the verb. Ps 95:7 → Trazei ao Senhor ×3, copying 28:1–2; passed the Latinist twice, no reader remarked.
vocative plural of persons, when the colon's build lets it be heard as an object (Afférte Dómino, fílii Dei: * afférte Dómino fílios aríetum)Ps 47 Ps 56 Ps 102 Ps 107ó + noun (Trazei ao Senhor, ó filhos de Deus)openPs 28:1: the Latin tells the vocative from the accusative by case, and the two cola are built alike; ó supplies the case. DRB O ye, MS1932 ó. Distinct from the Senhor vocative (glossary: no ó). Passed the Latinist twice. Ps 29:5 Psállite Dómino, sancti ejus → Entoai salmos ao Senhor, vós, seus santos: the same danger (bare, ao Senhor, seus santos is heard as a second dative); with a possessive, vós, marks it better than ó (ó seus santos is the option). The row's rule then: mark the vocative — ó before a bare noun, vós, before a possessive. Passed the Latinist twice; heard rightly. Ps 33:10 Timéte Dóminum, omnes sancti ejus → Temei o Senhor, vós, todos os seus santos — the row's vós, before the possessive (with omnes). The blind reader heard the vocative rightly, and 'santos' as the canonized saints first — the Latin's word.
aríescarneiro (filhos de carneiros)openPs 28:1 fílios aríetum (υἱοὺς κριῶν — the Latin's line with the Greek; the Hebrew doubles 'sons of God'): filhos kept for the psalm's play fílii Dei / fílios aríetum / fílius unicórnium (28:6). 64:14, 65:15, 113:4, 113:6 (grep). MS1932 tenros cordeiros explains. Ps 64:14 Indúti sunt aríetes óvium → Estão vestidos os carneiros das ovelhas (not DRB's 'flock'); no reader objected to the genitive. Ps 65:15 cum incénso aríetum → com incenso de carneiros (articles dropped for length) — the ambiguity reader heard 'incense plus rams'; the smoke of the sacrifice is the Latin's own compression, kept. Ps 113:4, 113:6 ut aríetes … sicut agni óvium → como carneiros … como cordeiros das ovelhas (64:14's genitive kept).
majéstasPs 71majestade (o Deus da majestade trovejou)workingPs 28:3; 71:19 (grep: the only other place). Kept apart from magnificéntia → magnificência (28:4).
intercíderePs 28dividir (A voz do Senhor que divide a chama de fogo)openPs 28:7 only (grep); L&S 'cut asunder, divide' citing this verse; διακόπτοντος; DRB divideth. cortar may be heard as putting the flame out; fender literary; MS1932 despede is the Hebrew's sense.
Vox Dómini + genitive participle (Vox Dómini confringéntis cedros, 28:5, 7, 9)Ps 28A voz do Senhor que quebra … (relative clause; the acclamation stays a noun phrase)openPs 28: the participles agree with Dómini; que can be heard with the voice or the Lord (the blind reader heard both). DRB and MS1932 make the voice the subject of a finite verb — the option.
diléctus (substantive)Ps 38 Ps 68 Ps 108o amadoopenPs 28:6 only (grep); ὁ ἠγαπημένος; who is meant stays open (MS1932's note reads Israel). o bem-amado the option. Needs a copula when a verb precedes it (the blind reader's zeugma). Ps 67:13 Rex virtútum dilécti, dilécti → O Rei dos poderes é do amado, do amado (DRB's copula; D43). Ps 83:2 the predicate Quam dilécta → Como são amadas (the row's root; amáveis, MS1932's familiar line, the option). The ambiguity reader heard 'loved by people' — the participle is open the same way in Latin.
dilúvium; inhabitáre facitPs 28 Ps 32 Ps 55 Ps 60 Ps 67dilúvio; fazer habitar (O Senhor faz habitar o dilúvio)openPs 28:10 (31:6 in dilúvio aquárum multárum; 67:7a qui inhabitáre facit — grep). The Latin's causative left open (who dwells); the blind reader heard the doubt, as the Latin has it; MS1932 faz do dilúvio a sua habitação decides. Ps 31:6b in dilúvio aquárum multárum → no dilúvio das muitas águas — applied. Ps 112:9 Qui habitáre facit stérilem in domo → Ele faz habitar numa casa a estéril — 67:6b's words and order (faz habitar numa casa …); the relative made a main verb after the stylist heard Ele, que … wait for a predicate.
dícere glóriamPs 5 Ps 7 Ps 14 Ps 16 Ps 18 Ps 20 Ps 21 Ps 23 Ps 25 Ps 28 Ps 29 Ps 44 Ps 48 Ps 51 Ps 56 Ps 65 Ps 72 Ps 86 Ps 90 Ps 107 Ps 111 Ps 112dizer glória (todos dirão glória)openPs 28:9 omnes dicent glóriam (πᾶς τις λέγει δόξαν): open between the object spoken and the cry. dirão: Glória! (the Hebrew's reading) and DRB his glory are options. No reader remarked.
super me (joy / gloating over someone)Ps 3 Ps 7 Ps 9 Ps 10 Ps 12 Ps 13 Ps 14 Ps 16 Ps 17 Ps 18 Ps 20 Ps 21 Ps 22 Ps 23 Ps 24 Ps 26 Ps 28 Ps 29 Ps 30 Ps 31 Ps 32 Ps 33 Ps 34 Ps 35 Ps 36 Ps 37 Ps 39 Ps 40 Ps 44 Ps 45 Ps 46 Ps 49 Ps 50 Ps 51 Ps 53 Ps 54 Ps 56 Ps 57 Ps 58 Ps 60 Ps 62 Ps 65 Ps 66 Ps 67 Ps 68 Ps 70 Ps 72 Ps 73 Ps 79 Ps 82 Ps 84 Ps 85 Ps 86 Ps 87 Ps 89 Ps 93 Ps 95 Ps 98 Ps 100 Ps 103 Ps 104 Ps 107 Ps 108 Ps 112 Ps 113 Ps 116 Ps 118 Ps 120à minha custa (e não alegrastes os meus inimigos à minha custa)openPs 29:2 (ἐπ᾽ ἐμέ). sobre mim after alegrar is heard as 'about me'; MS1932's idiom. Recurs in the family ne supergáudeant mihi (34:19, 34:24, 37:17 — grep before use). Passed the Latinist twice. Ps 34:19 and 34:24 supergáudeant mihi → Não se alegrem à minha custa. Hostile super me elsewhere in Ps 34 (34:16, 34:21, 34:26b) → contra mim; the scourges gathered super me (34:15) → sobre mim (physically upon). Ps 37:17 supergáudeant mihi → se alegrem à minha custa — the family's third place, applied. The Latinist asked exultem sobre mim twice (minor), the stylist once — refused (exultar is exsultáre's); the blind reader heard gloating first.
memória (of God, memóriæ sanctitátis ejus)Ps 29memória (dai graças à memória da sua santidade)openPs 29:5; 96:12 confitémini memóriæ sanctificatiónis ejus (another noun, grep). μνήμη. MS1932 celebrai a sua santa memória. The blind reader understood it. Ps 96:12 confitémini memóriæ sanctificatiónis ejus → dai graças à memória da sua santidade — 29:5b word for word, not 'with its own noun': the Greek of both is τῆς ἁγιωσύνης (checked in both parallels files), so D15's test merges sanctificátio here with sánctitas. The Latinist asked santificação twice (minor; the v2 gate conceded santidade is the sense) — held, option. 95:6 in sanctificatióne ejus is ἁγίασμα (sanctuary), another sense. The ambiguity reader heard a faint papal Sua Santidade (29:5 shares it). Ps 110:4 Memóriam fecit mirabílium suórum → Fez memória das suas maravilhas — the noun and the light verb kept; open between 'remembered' and 'left a remembrance', as the Latin (the ambiguity reader heard both). MS1932 instituiu um memorial (memoriále's word) the option.
indignátioPs 29 Ps 101indignação (há ira na sua indignação)workingPs 29:6 (θυμῷ); kept apart from ira → ira and furor → furor.
abundántiaPs 29 Ps 30 Ps 32 Ps 72abundância (na minha abundância)openPs 29:7 (εὐθηνία, 'prosperity'); 8 lines (grep: 32:17, 71:7, 77:25, 121:6, 121:7, 122:4, 144:7). The blind reader heard material goods first, well-being second — the Latin's range. MS1932 prosperidade the option. Ps 32:17 in abundántia autem virtútis suæ non salvábitur → e na abundância do seu poder não será salvo — the row's word, another place; passed the Latinist twice. Ps 72:12 abundántes in sǽculo (εὐθηνοῦντες, of persons) → prósperos no mundo — abundantes is heard as 'numerous' with persons; the row's option supplies the adjective. Passed the Latinist twice.
præstárePs 18dar (destes vigor ao meu esplendor)openPs 29:8 (παρέσχου); 18:8 sapiéntiam præstans (grep). conceder the option.
utílitasPs 29proveito (Que proveito há no meu sangue)openPs 29:10 only (grep; ὠφέλεια). MS1932 utilidade is heavy.
planctusPs 29lamento (Convertestes o meu lamento em júbilo)openPs 29:12 only (grep; κοπετός, the beating of the breast). Kept apart from fletus → pranto (29:6b, same psalm); MS1932 pranto merges them. DRB mourning → luto the option.
saccusPs 29pano de saco (rasgastes o meu pano de saco)openPs 29:12 only (grep; σάκκον). o meu saco is a bag in Portuguese and a vulgarity in Brazil; pano de saco keeps the word and says cloth, without explaining the mourning (MS1932's parenthesis (de penitência)). The blind reader listed it as unknown but heard 'a coarse cloth I wore'. cilícium (34:13, 68:12) is another word → cilício.
glória mea (the self)Ps 5 Ps 7 Ps 14 Ps 16 Ps 18 Ps 20 Ps 21 Ps 23 Ps 25 Ps 28 Ps 29 Ps 44 Ps 48 Ps 51 Ps 56 Ps 65 Ps 72 Ps 86 Ps 90 Ps 107 Ps 111 Ps 112a minha glória (Para que a minha glória vos cante)openPs 29:13; 56:9 = 107:3 Exsúrge, glória mea, 107:2 in glória mea (grep; 3:4, 61:8 are of God). Not explained (MS1932 a minha alma). The blind reader heard honour personified, or the self. Ps 56:9 Exsúrge, glória mea, exsúrge, psaltérium et cíthara → Levanta-te, minha glória, levanta-te, saltério e cítara — tu, the Latin's one singular for glory and instruments (MS1932 the same). The blind reader heard God first and the tu then clashed; the vós reading (Levantai-vos … levanta-te) is an option. 107:3 copies it. Ps 61:8 In Deo salutáre meum, et glória mea → Em Deus está a minha salvação, e a minha glória (of God; an Alleluia, 10-09, and a Matins antiphon).
clamábo … deprecábor (two futures ending both cola)Ps 29 Ps 89hei de clamar … suplicareiopenPs 29:9: clamarei / suplicarei rhymed at mediant and final (the stylist); the periphrastic future is the same tense.
tentárePs 25 Ps 34 Ps 94experimentar where God tests the psalmist (Provai-me, Senhor, e experimentai-me); tentar where men tempt GodopenPs 25:2 tenta me — draft 1's tentai-me was heard by the blind reader first as "lead me into sin"; experimentar is free and kept apart from provar (probáre) in the same colon, safe at the vós imperative (past experimentei). Where men tempt God (77:18, 77:41, 77:56, 94:8 tentavérunt me … probavérunt, 105:14; grep) tentar is heard rightly and can stay; 34:16 tentavérunt me (men trying the psalmist) decides there; the noun tentátio 17:30, 94:8. Ps 34:16 tentavérunt me (men trying the psalmist) → puseram-me à prova (Matos Soares 1932): draft 1's tentaram-me was heard first by the blind reader as 'tried to lead me into sin' — the 25:2 fault again. Passed the Latinist. So the row has three: experimentar (God tests), tentar (men tempt God), pôr à prova (men try a man). Ps 94:8 tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt me → os vossos pais me tentaram, me provaram; diem tentatiónis → o dia da tentação — the row applied (men tempting God). The ambiguity reader heard the noun tentação as the people being tempted (or Christ's temptation), and provaram possibly as 'tasted'; kept — the Latin tentátio is as open. Passed the Latinist twice.
in concílio / ecclésia sedérePs 1 Ps 21 Ps 25 Ps 39sentar-se no … (Não me sentei no conselho da vaidade)openPs 25:4; the preposition em, not com, so the body is heard and not advice (the blind reader). 1:1 in cáthedra pestiléntiæ non sedit is another build.
illuminátioPs 26 Ps 43 Ps 118luz (O Senhor é a minha luz e a minha salvação)openPs 26:1 (the Monday Prime antiphon; Introits) — God named as the one who gives light; iluminação makes him a process and is heard as lighting. Cost: lumen → luz too; they never meet in a verse (grep), but 4:7 lumen vultus tui and 43:4, 89:8 illuminátio vultus tui are near-formulas and may keep them apart with iluminação (free). DRB light, MS1932 luz. Ps 43:4b e a luz do vosso rosto: the row held — the Latinist asked iluminação twice (minor), refused (26:1; heard as lighting); option kept in Ps 43's decision illuminatio. 89:8 will meet the same request. Ps 89:8 in illuminatióne vultus tui → à luz do vosso rosto — as foreseen, the v2 Latinist asked iluminação (minor); held under this row, as 43:4b.
nocéntes (participle as noun)Ps 18 Ps 28 Ps 34malfeitores (os malfeitores)openPs 26:2 (κακοῦντας); only other place 34:1 Júdica, Dómine, nocéntes me, where the object may ask for os que me fazem mal. Apart from malígnus → malvado (D24), iníquus → iníquo, ímpius → ímpio. Ps 34:1 Júdica, Dómine, nocéntes me → Julgai, Senhor, os que me fazem mal — the object asked for the clause, as the row foresaw (Matos Soares 1932 word for word; DRB 'them that wrong me'). The Introit / Tract of Passion Monday. Passed the Latinist twice.
castraPs 11 Ps 26 Ps 72 Ps 117acampamento (Se um acampamento se instalar contra mim)openPs 26:3 (παρεμβολή; the Eastertide responsory, Pasc2-3.txt); the Latin names the camp, not the army. consístere → instalar-se here (the stylist wanted the subject first; postar unknown to the blind reader and heard today as posting online). 26:3b turned the same way (Se uma batalha se levantar contra mim). Other castra: 77:28, 105:16 (grep before copying).
voluptasPs 26 Ps 35delícias (as delícias do Senhor)openPs 26:4b; 35:9 torrénte voluptátis tuæ. deleite is delectátio's, doçura dulcédo's, prazer heard first as the senses' (and 25:3 has achei prazer for complacére). The Latinist (minor) wants the singular o prazer; refused, the plural is the idiom (number is grammar), a delícia an option. delíciæ 138:11 decides there. Ps 35:9 torrénte voluptátis tuæ → da torrente das vossas delícias — the Latinist asked the singular twice (draft 1 da vossa delícia, the gate do vosso deleite); refused both times, as at 26:4b. da vossa delícia is an option in Ps 35's decision potabis.
in abscóndito (a hidden place)Ps 9 Ps 16 Ps 26 Ps 30 Ps 34 Ps 43 Ps 80no lugar escondido (protegeu-me no lugar escondido da sua tenda)openPs 26:5, keeping abscóndit … in abscóndito (ἔκρυψεν … ἐν ἀποκρύφῳ) one root; esconderijo is latíbulum's (17:12) — the stylist's word, refused, an option; 9:30a's adverbial às escondidas is another use. 30:21 Abscóndes eos in abscóndito faciéi tuæ should follow. Ps 30:21 Abscóndes eos in abscóndito faciéi tuæ → Vós os escondereis no lugar escondido da vossa face — as this row asked; the psalm's four abscond- words are all esconder (30:5, 20, 21 ×2). The blind reader heard 'a secret shelter of God' first; passed the Latinist twice.
petraPs 26 Ps 39 Ps 77 Ps 104rocha (Sobre uma rocha me exaltou)openPs 26:6; lapis → pedra (117:22). Indefinite, as the Latin has no article. 60:3 In petra exaltásti me should copy. 12 other lines (grep: 39:3, 60:3, 77:15, 77:16, 77:20, 80:17, 103:12, 103:17, 104:41, 113:8, 136:9, 140:6). Ps 60:3 in petra exaltásti me → sobre uma rocha me exaltastes — copied from 26:6 as the row asked; the stylist's sobre a rocha refused. Ps 80:17 et de petra → e da rocha — definite here: the rock of the desert, and de uma rocha would be any rock. No reader remarked. 77:15–16, 104:41, 113:8 (the same rock) may want the same. Ps 113:8 petram … et rupem → a rocha … e o penhasco — rupes (ἀκρότομος) kept apart; see the new row rupes.
hóstiaPs 26 Ps 95 Ps 115vítima (uma vítima de aclamação)openPs 26:6b; the cognate hóstia is heard first as the Host, sacrifício is sacrifícium's (115:17 tibi sacrificábo hóstiam laudis, DO id 115:7b, has both roots, so they must differ). The blind reader heard vítima as someone harmed (he did not know imolei) — the cost, recorded. Other hóstia: 95:8 Tóllite hóstias, 115:17 (DO id 115:7b) — grep. Ps 95:8 Tóllite hóstias → Tomai vítimas (MS1932; the Latinist, minor on v1). v1 Erguei vítimas (= 23:7 Attóllite → Erguei, one Greek ἄρατε) was heard by the ambiguity reader as 'help the victims of harm'; so tomar now serves tóllere here and súmere at 80:3 (λάβετε), against D15's test, for a right first hearing. The stylist asked the article (as vítimas), option. v2 gate clean. Ps 115:7b tibi sacrificábo hóstiam laudis → a vós sacrificarei uma hóstia de louvor — a local departure from vítima, proposed for a ruling across 26:6b, 95:8, 115:7b. v1 had uma vítima de louvor; the stylist ('victim of praise', worst line) and the ambiguity reader (sacrificial sense unknown) both faulted it, as the Ps 26 blind reader had. hóstia is the Latin's own word and MS1932's; and here the Church reads the verse of the Host (Corpus Christi Vespers antiphon Cálicem salutáris accípiam: et sacrificábo hóstiam laudis, DO Pent01-4), so the first hearing this row feared is, in this psalm, the liturgy's own. The v2 Latinist gate passed it. Four blind readers have now stumbled on vítima; for the main session: either move the row to hóstia everywhere, or keep 115:7b as the one exception (uma vítima is option 1 there).
vociferátioPs 26 Ps 32aclamaçãoopenPs 26:6b hóstiam vociferatiónis; 32:3 bene psállite ei in vociferatióne can follow. ἀλαλαγμός, the shout. júbilo left to gáudium / jubilátio (46:6). Ps 32:3 bene psállite ei in vociferatióne → entoai-lhe bem os salmos com aclamação — the row followed; passed the Latinist twice; heard rightly.
viríliter ágerePs 26 Ps 30portar-se como homem (porta-te como homem)openPs 26:14; 30:25 Viríliter ágite → Portai-vos como homens (only the two, grep). Draft 1 had MS1932's porta-te varonilmente: the blind reader did not know varonilmente, the stylist (worst line) called it bookish and asked age como homem; his como homem taken (the Latin's vir), the verb kept for 30:25, where Agi is also 'I acted' (rule 3). Ps 30:25 Viríliter ágite → Portai-vos como homens — applied as proposed (Agi is 'I acted'); the blind reader heard 'be brave' first, 'as males' second. Passed the Latinist twice; no stylist remark.
silére / tacérePs 27 Ps 34 Ps 49ficar em silêncio / calar-se (não fiqueis em silêncio comigo: * para que não vos caleis comigo)openPs 27:1 — two Latin verbs where the Greek has one twice (παρασιωπάω); kept two (rule 1); a me → comigo (the Brazilian idiom: silent towards me). Other places (grep before copying): 34:22, 38:3, 38:13, 49:3, 49:20, 82:2, 106:29–30, 108:2, 31:3 (grep). No reader remarked. Ps 31:3 Quóniam tácui → Porque me calei — applied. Ps 34:22 Vidísti, Dómine, ne síleas → Vós vistes, Senhor, não fiqueis em silêncio — applied; the Passiontide responsory; the stylist's best line. Ps 38:3 sílui a bonis → fiquei em silêncio quanto às coisas boas (draft 1 sobre coisas boas: topic, refused by the Latinist and the stylist; draft 2 longe do bem: spatial, refused at the gate; quanto às is the gate's fix and keeps both readings — withheld even good things / silent about them). Both readers asked for calar-se — refused, tacére's verb, and 38:13b Ne síleas → Não fiqueis em silêncio (= 34:22) is the same Latin verb. Ps 49:3 et non silébit → e não ficará em silêncio; 49:20 et tácui → e eu me calei — the two verbs kept apart in one psalm (the Greek differs too: παρασιωπήσεται / ἐσίγησα). The stylist asked se calará at 49:3 — option. Ps 82:2 Ne táceas, neque compescáris → Não vos caleis, nem vos contenhais (compéscere, new row). Ps 108:2 laudem meam ne tacúeris → não caleis o meu louvor (transitive calar, MS1932; decision tacueris) — the reflexive row needs a preposition here, and laudem meam stays open (my praise of God / God's word for me). The v2 Latinist asked não vos caleis ao meu louvor — option.
adinvéntioPs 27 Ps 76 Ps 80 Ps 98invenções (segundo a maldade das suas invenções)openPs 27:4; six lines (27:4, 76:13 God's in adinventiónibus tuis, 80:13, 98:8, 105:29, 105:39) — must serve God's works too, so not maquinações; the blind reader heard schemes (the sense, from maldade). Ps 76:13 in adinventiónibus tuis (God's) → nas vossas invenções — the test this row named. The v1 stylist's worst line ('gadgets, fabrications'; asked desígnios, consílium's word, D33) and odd / unknown to the ambiguity reader. Held; for Gustavo — a row that must serve God's devisings and men's. Ps 80:13 ibunt in adinventiónibus suis → caminharão nas suas invenções — the row; no reader objected; the ambiguity reader heard 'their own ideas', once 'idols they made'. Ps 98:8 adinventiónes eórum → as invenções deles (deles ties them to eis, Moses, Aaron, Samuel); the ambiguity reader heard 'inventions', then 'lies'. Held. Ps 105:29 irritavérunt eum in adinventiónibus suis → o provocaram com as suas invenções; 105:39 se prostituíram nas suas invenções — the row applied (preposition by the verb). The ambiguity reader heard the sense of evil devices only half.
salvátioPs 24 Ps 27 Ps 32salvações (o protetor das salvações do seu Cristo)openPs 27:8 only (grep), plural for σωτηρίων, as 17:51 salútes → salvações; the blind reader doubted the plural — the Latin's.
ex voluntáte meaPs 1 Ps 5 Ps 15 Ps 20 Ps 27 Ps 29 Ps 39 Ps 50 Ps 53 Ps 67 Ps 72 Ps 102 Ps 110 Ps 118de minha própria vontade (e de minha própria vontade lhe darei graças)openPs 27:7b (ἐκ θελήματός μου); draft 1 de minha vontade sounded incomplete to the stylist; própria completes the idiom and ex → de stays; de livre vontade is voluntárie's (53:8).

reveréri / reveréntiaPs 34 Ps 39 Ps 67 Ps 110 Ps 112ser desonrado / desonra (Sejam envergonhados e desonrados; Vistam-se de vergonha e de desonra)open — for a rulingPs 34:4, 34:26, 34:26b (ἐντρέπεσθαι / ἐντροπή: to be abashed); always beside confúndi or erubéscere, so it needs a third word of shame (confúndi → ser envergonhado, D15; erubéscere → corar). eugePs 34 Ps 39 Ps 69Que bom (Que bom, que bom, os nossos olhos viram)openPs 34:21, 34:25 (εὖγε), in the mouths of gloaters. Draft 1 Bem feito (said of another's misfortune): the stylist and the blind reader heard 'deserved punishment' at 34:25. 34:25 ánimæ nostræ → para a nossa alma. 39:16 and 69:4 qui dicunt mihi: Euge, euge (grep) should copy. Ps 39:16 copied: os que me dizem: Que bom, que bom. The stylist ('sounds sincere and cheerful, not jeering') and the blind reader ('the mockery may be missed') both failed it; the stylist asked Bem feito again. Held for the row; the recurring complaint is noted for the ruling (69:4 still to copy). Ps 69:4b copied os que me dizem: Que bom, que bom (rule 6, = 39:16) — and all three v1 readers failed it again (Latinist minor twice, 'weakens the taunt'; stylist 'warm and approving'; ambiguity reader 'the mockery is not audible'): five readers of five across Pss 39 and 69. Proposal for a ruling: Bem feito, bem feito in all four places (34:21, 34:25, 39:16, 69:4b) — said by mockers to me (qui dicunt mihi), 'serves you right' is exactly the gloat; the 34:25 mishearing ('deserved punishment') is the same sense seen from outside. The v2 Latinist offered Muito bem, muito bem; option in Ps 69's decision euge.

Ps 55:9b tunc converténtur inimíci mei retrórsum → então os meus inimigos voltarão para trás — as this row foresaw; heard as retreat. Ps 49:17 projecísti sermónes meos retrórsum → lançaste para trás as minhas palavras. Ps 69:4 Avertántur retrórsum → Voltem para trás (as 34:4b, 39:15b). 69:4b Avertántur without retrórsum → Voltem-se (the verb kept; bare voltem is 'come back', D44): retreat heard as likely by the ambiguity reader, conversion possible. The stylist's Voltem-se para trás for both refused (turning round, not retreat).
æmuláriPs 36 Ps 77ter inveja de (Não tenhas inveja dos malvados)openPs 36:1, 36:7, 36:8 (παραζηλόω ×3; one phrase three times; 36:8 without an object: não tenhas inveja, a ponto de fazeres o mal). History: segundo o vosso dito was tested in Ps 118:33–80 and refused by the stylist in all six places where the singular stands ("a quoted phrase", "bookish", "guardar um dito is to keep a phrase in memory"; he asks for palavra). The blind reader understood it everywhere; the Latinist passed it. It stays in the text under D15 — for the main session to revisit; fall-backs segundo a vossa promessa (fails 118:67) or the merge into palavra (collapses this formula into secúndum verbum tuum, 7 verses away at 118:58 / 65). 118:116: the formula drew no remark from the stylist (his own proposed line keeps it) nor from the blind reader; the Latinist (draft 10, minor) notes that dissestes dates an utterance the noun leaves timeless — D16's named cost 118:133, 170 (the formula) and 118:169 (juxta → conforme o que dissestes; the Latin varies the preposition and Portuguese has the plain pair conforme / segundo): no remark from the stylist on either of two readings, understood by the blind reader twice; the Latinist's minor (past tense) on drafts 13–14, silence on 15–16. 118:154 propter elóquium tuum → pelo que dissestes (not por causa do, which echoed a minha causa in the same verse).

The stylist called atender em not Portuguese and asked Acudi em meu auxílio; the blind reader heard 'come to my help' first; the Latinist passed it twice. For the coordinator before Ps 69: the versicle of every Hour will say whatever is ruled here. Ps 39:14 is not this formula: Compláceat tibi … ut éruas me: * Dómine, ad adjuvándum me réspice has neither inténde nor adjutórium; it shares only Dómine, ad adjuvándum me with 69:2b (→ auxiliar-me, the adjuváre row). D40 stays open. Ps 69:2 translated with 37:23's wording held: Deus, atendei em meu auxílio: * Senhor, apressai-vos para auxiliar-me — D40 still unruled, so the holding ruling keeps the two psalms one. The v1 stylist failed atender em again ('not Portuguese', asked voltai-vos em, refused: convértere's verb); the ambiguity reader understood a plea to come and help; the Latinist passed it twice. Options in Ps 69's decision intende: acudi, vinde (DM1962, the line Brazilians know), atendei ao, voltai-vos. D40 is now the one open question in Ps 69.

Doublets

13 / 52 · 39:14–18 / 69 · 56:8–12 + 59:7–14 / 107. Whoever translates the second copies the first wherever the Latin is identical, and says so in audit.
